confirmedFindings.title: Flat insight feed ranks by strokes_impact×confidence, but every Tier-1 generator hard-codes both to 0 — real counterfactual-backed insights always score 0
confirmedFindings.evidence: rankScore: `const impact = Math.abs(Number(insight.evidence.strokes_impact ?? 0)); const confidence = Number(insight.evidence.confidence ?? 0); return impact * confidence;`. Every Tier-1 generator sets `strokes_impact: 0` AND `confidence: 0` (verified in putt-distance.ts:138/140, scrambling.ts:109/111, par-type.ts:108/110, course-mgmt.ts:119/121, pressure-gap.ts:131/133, warmup-hole.ts:134/136, approach-miss.ts:203/205, putt-bias.ts:150/152, tee-strategy.ts:213/215). generator-base.ts:129-142 injects `counterfactual` + `standing` but never overwrites strokes_impact/confidence. The REAL stroke value lives in evidence.counterfactual.strokes_saved_per_round, which rankScore never reads.
confirmedFindings.impact: On the coach dashboard (getInsightsForCoach) and the player Hub signal card (getTopInsightForPlayer), every standing/counterfactual-backed Tier-1 insight scores exactly 0×0=0. The 'top insight' a coach/player sees is whichever composite happens to carry a non-zero strokes_impact, not the genuinely highest-leverage skill gap. A player whose biggest real leak is, say, a 0.8 strokes/round putting gap will never see it surfaced as the top signal because its rank score is 0.
confirmedFindings.fix: Make rankScore fall back to evidence.counterfactual?.strokes_saved_per_round (when not suppressed) when strokes_impact is 0, and use a sensible default confidence for Tier-1 rows (or compute confidence from confidence_factors instead of hard-coding 0). Alternatively, have generator-base.ts copy counterfactual.strokes_saved_per_round into evidence.strokes_impact and derive confidence from the confidence_factors product before upsert.

Verdict: confirmed. Per the rubric (critical = wrong number/data loss; high = misleading/materially degraded), this is HIGH rather than the claimed CRITICAL.

confirmedFindings.title: long_approach_3putt and short_approach_proximity_gap test/display approach_miss.your_value as FEET, but it is a green-hit PERCENT after the unit-inflation redesign
confirmedFindings.evidence: long-approach: `// For approach_miss the lower-better unit is feet; >50 ft is weak vs Tour 45 ft\n Number(i.evidence.your_value ?? 0) > 50` then `your_value_display: \`${proximity} ft\``. But approach-miss.ts:194 sets `your_value: agg.green_hit_pct` (a 0-100 percent — line 130 `greenHitPct = (100 * greenHitN) / inBucket.length`). short-approach: `const yourVal = Number(i.evidence.your_value ?? 0); return yourVal > 22;` then renders `${proximity} ft from the hole`. Both rules are LIVE-registered (composite/index.ts:37-38).
confirmedFindings.impact: The threshold semantics are inverted: long_approach fires when green-hit% > 50% (i.e. GOOD reach), the opposite of 'weak proximity'; short_approach fires when green-hit% > 22% (almost always true). When fired, the card tells the coach '175+ yd approaches average 65 ft from the hole' or '50-125 yd you're leaving the ball 65 ft from the hole' where 65 is actually a green-hit percent — a fabricated, nonsensical proximity. comparison vs 'Tour ~18 ft'/'45 ft' makes the player look catastrophically worse than reality.
confirmedFindings.fix: approach_miss no longer exposes proximity feet in evidence.your_value. Either (a) add evidence.proximity_when_hit_feet to the approach-miss evidence and have the composites read that field with the MIN_GREENS_FOR_PROXIMITY guard, flipping the threshold to a LOW green-hit% OR a HIGH proximity; or (b) retire these two composites until a real standing-backed proximity-in-feet metric ships. At minimum stop labeling a percent as 'ft'.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced every element from the actual code on the live path.

SOURCE OF THE PERCENT: src/lib/coachhelm/v3/generators/approach-miss.ts:194 sets `your_value: agg.green_hit_pct` with `unit: 'percent'` (line 193); green_hit_pct = `(100 * greenHitN) / inBucket.length` (line 130) — a 0-100 percent. The on-green proximity in feet is computed (proximity_when_hit_feet, line 134-137) but is NOT placed in `evidence` at all (evidence block lines 190-211 only exposes green_hit_pct). This is the P1b "reach vs dial-in" redesign.

COMPOSITES STILL READ IT AS FEET:
- long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts:16-23 — `isWeakLongApproach` does `Number(i.evidence.your_value ?? 0) > 50` with the comment "For approach_miss the lower-better unit is feet; >50 ft is weak vs Tour 45 ft". It passes the value through as `approach_proximity_ft` (line 45) and renders `${proximity} ft` (lines 57, 69) vs comparison_value 45 "PGA Tour 175+ yd avg".
- short-approach-proximity-gap.ts:14-21 — `isWeakShortApproach` does `yourVal > 22`; renders `${proximity} ft from the hole` (line 54) and `${proximity} ft avg` (line 65) vs "Tour ~18 ft" (line 67).

INVERTED/NONSENSE SEMANTICS CONFIRMED: long fires when green-hit% > 50 (that is GOOD reach, opposite of "weak proximity"); short fires when green-hit% > 22 (nearly always true). When fired, a green-hit percent (e.g. 65) is printed as "65 ft from the hole" against "Tour ~18 ft / 45  ft" — a fabricated proximity that makes the player look far worse than reality.

LIVE PATH CONFIRMED: both rules registered in composite/index.ts:37-38; synthesis.ts runs COMPOSITE_RULES and upserts via upsertInsightV3 to golf_coach_insights; orchestrator.ts:307 calls synthesizeForPlayer(playerId) immediately after the three ApproachMissGenerator runs (orchestrator.ts:252-254), and orchestrator.analyzePlayer is the live entrypoint reached from generateTeamInsights/analyzePlayer in src/app/golf/actions/insights.ts. Tier-1 signature is prefixed `v3:` (generator-base.ts:150) → `v3:approach_miss:175_plus_ft`, so the composites' `signature.includes('175_plus_ft')`/`'50_125ft')` matches. Not behind any disabled flag.

GIT EVIDENCE OF THE DRIFT: approach-miss.ts last touched by `0c1d0f2d fix(coachhelm): approach insight = green-hit% (reach) + on-green proximity (P1b)` (the redesign that flipped your_value from feet to percent), while the composite rules were last written in `572b2c8d W28: composite insights v1` — authored against the pre-redesign feet contract and never updated. The composite comments still assert "the lower-better unit is feet," which is now false.

NUANCE ON SEVERITY: each rule has an AND co-condition (weak mid-putt team_pct<50 for long; weak scrambling team_pct<40 for short), so they do not fire for every player — but when they do fire the displayed number and Tour comparison are genuinely wrong and coach-facing. That matches claimed high (misleading user-acted claim) rather than critical (which would require always-wrong). Claimed severity high and live=true both upheld; confidence is solidly above the reporter's 0.85.

CONFIRMED on the live path with strong golf-domain impact. I verified the full chain end to end.

CORE FACT (confirmed): approach-miss.ts:194 sets `your_value: agg.green_hit_pct` with `unit: 'percent'` (line 192-194), where green_hit_pct = `(100 * greenHitN) / inBucket.length` (line 130) — a 0-100 PERCENT. The actual proximity in feet (`proximity_when_hit_feet`) lives ONLY on the generator aggregate (lines 101/150) and is used solely in the prose/title (line 160); grep confirms it is NEVER written into the persisted evidence object. generator-base.ts:113-154 persists exactly `composed.evidence`, and ApproachMissGenerator has requiresStanding=false (line 110), so no downstream field rewrites it. Therefore the only proximity-ish field the composites can read (`i.evidence.your_value`) is a percent.

BOTH RULES ARE LIVE: index.ts:37-38 registers longApproach3Putt and shortApproachGap; synthesis.ts runs rule.detect() then upserts (lines 74-129); orchestrator.ts:307 calls synthesizeForPlayer inside analyzePlayer; insights.ts:833 (generateInsightsForTeam) calls analyzePlayer; orchestrator.ts:252-254 registers all three ApproachMissGenerator buckets as Tier-1. Signature matching works: generator writes `approach_miss:175_plus_ft`/`approach_miss:50_125ft` (approach-miss.ts:189), and the rules `.includes('175_plus_ft')`/`.includes('50_125ft')` match those substrings. The read path (insight-delivery.ts:808-809, 916-917) serves title/content verbatim, so the broken prose reaches the user unaltered.

GOLF-DOMAIN VALIDATION OF IMPACT:
1. Inverted thresholds. long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts:20-21 comments "the lower-better unit is feet; >50 ft is weak vs Tour 45 ft" and fires on `your_value > 50`. But the value is a green-hit PERCENT where HIGHER is better. Per the domain doc (v3-research-golf-domain.md:254-255), 175+ yd college/Tour GIR is ~50%, so green_hit_pct > 50 means the player is ABOVE-average at finding greens from long range — the rule fires on GOOD reach and labels it a "weak long approach." short-approach-proximity-gap.ts:19-20 fires on green_hit_pct > 22, and 50-125 yd college GIR is ~75%+ (doc:254), so this is satisfied virtually always.
2. Fabricated, alarming coaching numbers. When fired, the cards render `${proximity} ft` where proximity = round(green_hit_pct). A player hitting 65% of long greens sees "your 175+ yd approaches average 65 ft from the hole" vs the real "PGA Tour 45 ft" (long-approach lines 57/71); a player hitting 78% of short greens sees "From 50-125 yd you're leaving the ball 78 ft from the hole (Tour is ~18 ft)" (short-approach lines 54-55, with the genuine 16-19 ft Tour anchor from doc:88). The comparison anchors (45 ft, 18 ft) are REAL Tour proximities, which makes the juxtaposition maximally misleading — it tells the coach/player their wedge/long-iron proximity is ~3-4x worse than Tour when it is in fact normal or good, and prescribes "dial in your stock 200-yd shot"/"tighten wedge distance control" — concrete practice prescriptions a coach would act on based on a nonsense number. This is exactly the unit-integrity failure class the approach-miss redesign header (lines 21-27) claimed to fix; the composites were not updated to the post-redesign percent semantics.

This is not cosmetic. It produces a wrong, action-driving coaching number and an inverted firing condition on a live, user-visible card. The claimed severity (high) is correct — I considered critical, but it sits just below: the cards only fire when a co-leg (weak mid-putt for long; weak scrambling team_pct<40 for short) also exists, so it is conditional rather than guaranteed, and the broken value is a derived display rather than e.g. a persisted strokes-gained figure feeding other math. High is the right call. The proposed fix (add proximity_when_hit_feet to evidence and have the composites read it with the MIN_GREENS_FOR_PROXIMITY guard, flipping the threshold to LOW green-hit% or HIGH proximity; or retire the two composites until a real proximity-in-feet metric ships; at minimum stop labeling a percent as 'ft') is sound and domain-correct.

CONFIRMED. I independently traced the full live path and could not find any guard that neutralizes the bug.

Generator side (the percent): src/lib/coachhelm/v3/generators/approach-miss.ts:130 computes `greenHitPct = (100 * greenHitN) / inBucket.length` (a 0-100 percent), then line 194 sets `your_value: agg.green_hit_pct` with line 192 `unit: 'percent'`. The real feet value lives in a SEPARATE field, `proximity_when_hit_feet` (line 150), which the composites never read. The generator's own header (lines 21-29) documents that the unit-inflation redesign deliberately moved proximity-feet out of your_value.

Composite side (treats it as feet): 
- long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts:16-22 `isWeakLongApproach` matches `insight_type === 'approach_miss'` + `signature.includes('175_plus_ft')` + `Number(i.evidence.your_value ?? 0) > 50` with the comment "the lower-better unit is feet; >50 ft is weak". It then renders at line 57 `Your 175+ yd approaches average ${proximity} ft from the hole` and line 69 `your_value_display: \`${proximity} ft\`` vs comparison_value 45 (Tour feet).
- short-approach-proximity-gap.ts:14-21 `isWeakShortApproach` matches `approach_miss` + `signature.includes('50_125ft')` + `yourVal > 22`, then line 54 renders `From 50-125 yd you're leaving the ball ${proximity} ft from the hole on average (Tour is ~18 ft)` and line 65 `${proximity} ft avg`.

Round-trip survives: generator signature is `approach_miss:${agg.bucket}` (approach-miss.ts:189), so `.includes('175_plus_ft')`/`.includes('50_125ft')` match. The loader (composite/loader.ts:23-26) selects `signature` and `evidence` verbatim; synthesis.ts:74-77 calls each rule's detect with those rows untransformed; detect reads `i.evidence.your_value` directly. No coercion, no unit check.

Live registration & invocation: composite/index.ts:37-38 registers both rules in COMPOSITE_RULES. The v2 orchestrator (the live engine) instantiates all three ApproachMissGenerator buckets (orchestrator.ts:252-254), runs the Tier-1 batch (runTier1, line 271), then calls synthesizeForPlayer (line 307) which evaluates the composites against the freshly-written rows. The read path (insight-delivery.ts) filters only on status != dismissed and does not exclude composites. The composite content/title are pre-baked plain-text strings persisted to golf_coach_insights and shown verbatim; there is no prose sanitizer that catches a percent-mislabeled-as-feet.

Skeptic tests I ran, all of which FAILED to kill the finding:
1. Signature-mismatch gate? No — `.includes()` matches the `approach_miss:<bucket>` signature.
2. Downstream sanitizer/unit guard? None found; content is verbatim prose.
3. Read-path filter? Only status-based; composites surfaced.
4. Co-condition neutralizes it? No. short_approach requires scrambling team_pct < 40 AND green_hit_pct > 22 — the >22 condition is true for essentially every 50-125 yd bucket (real green-hit rates 60-85%), so a weak-scrambling player with a healthy green-hit% gets told "you're leaving the ball 80 ft from the hole (Tour ~18 ft)" — a fabricated, alarming, wrong stat. long_approach requires a weak 10-15ft putter (team_pct < 50) AND green_hit_pct > 50; that fires for the STRONGER long-iron players (threshold inverted vs intent) and renders e.g. "55 ft" vs "PGA 45 ft". Both produce a concrete wrong number the coach is explicitly told to act on ("dial in your stock 200-yd shot", "tighten wedge distance control").

The threshold semantics ARE inverted as claimed, but the more damaging, certain defect is the unit mislabel: a 0-100 percent rendered as "ft" and compared to Tour feet anchors. This is exactly the class of "unit inflation" bug the redesign was supposed to fix — the generator was fixed but these two composites were never updated to read the new proximity_when_hit_feet field.

Severity: the claimed 'high' is correct, arguably conservative. It produces a fabricated user-facing number on the live path with no guard, and the prose drives a coaching action. I keep it at high rather than escalating to critical only because firing requires a co-condition (not every player) and these approach_miss rows are flagged diagnostic (requiresStanding=false) — but the rendered claim itself is unambiguously wrong when it appears.

confirmedFindings.title: v3 approach-miss onGreenFinishFeet ×3's null/unknown distance_unit_after — inverse of the v2 default, re-introducing 3× proximity inflation
confirmedFindings.evidence: `return s.distance_unit_after === 'feet' ? Number(s.distance_to_hole_after) : Number(s.distance_to_hole_after) * 3;` — a null/undefined/other unit falls to the else and is multiplied by 3. The v2 calculator does the SAFE inverse: normalizeToFeet (golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:416-418) `unit === 'yards' ? distance * 3 : distance` — null is treated as already-feet (no multiply). distance_unit_after is `.optional()` in the write schema (golf.ts:368) and documented 'mixed in prod' (shot-source.ts:27), so null on-green rows exist.
confirmedFindings.impact: An on-green finish (genuinely feet) stored with a null unit gets tripled (e.g. a real 20 ft proximity becomes 60 ft) in the approach-miss title/prose ('63 ft when you do', exactly the artifact the redesign claims to have killed). Diagnostic-only (requiresStanding=false) so it doesn't poison a counterfactual, but the displayed proximity number a coach reads is wrong for null-unit rows.
confirmedFindings.fix: Match the v2 convention: treat a non-'yards' unit (incl. null) as already feet — `s.distance_unit_after === 'yards' ? value * 3 : value`. Since off-green misses are already excluded, the only ×3 case should be an explicit 'yards' on-green legacy row.

One imprecision in the finding (not a defect): the comment's claim that off-green misses are 'excluded upstream' is inaccurate — loadApproachShots returns all approach shots; the on-green filter happens IN the generator via `greenShots = inBucket.filter(reachedGreen)` (line 128) and onGreenFinishFeet only runs over greenShots (line 136). Net effect is identical to what the finding describes: only on-green finishes are tripled, and a null-unit on-green finish is wrongly ×3'd.

Severity: medium is correct. It produces a wrong displayed proximity number a coach reads (e.g., 20 ft → 60 ft) for the null-unit-on-green subset, which is misleading, but it is diagnostic-only (no counterfactual/standing impact) and the affected subset (null unit AND on-green) is narrower than the general miss population. The standard data-entry path sets an explicit unit, so this primarily bites legacy/imported/optional-write rows. Confidence ~0.8.

VERIFIED end-to-end on the live path. The cited code exists exactly as quoted at src/lib/coachhelm/v3/generators/approach-miss.ts:90-92: `return s.distance_unit_after === 'feet' ? Number(s.distance_to_hole_after) : Number(s.distance_to_hole_after) * 3;`. The else-branch (×3) fires for null/undefined/any-non-'feet' unit. This is the INVERSE of the project's established normalization convention in src/lib/utils/golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:416-418 `normalizeToFeet(...) { if (distance == null) return 0; return unit === 'yards' ? distance * 3 : distance; }` — which treats null as already-feet (no multiply). (Note: the auditor's path for the v2 calculator was slightly off — it lives at src/lib/utils/golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts, not coachhelm/v2 — but the function, line numbers, and logic are exactly as cited.)

LIVE-PATH confirmed: generateInsightsForTeam (insights.ts:833) → coachHelmIntelligence.analyzePlayer → orchestrator.ts:252-254 instantiates `new ApproachMissGenerator(playerId, bucket).run()` for all 3 buckets (the W25-cutover comment at orchestrator.ts:17-18 confirms the v3 generators are live and replaced the v2 ones). aggregate() averages onGreenFinishFeet over green-finding shots (approach-miss.ts:136) and the value flows DIRECTLY into user-facing prose: the title `${prox.toFixed(0)} ft when you do` (line 165) and the dial-in sentence "you finish ${prox} ft from the hole (Tour ~${tourProx} ft)" (line 175).

A real 20 ft proximity on a null-unit row is tripled to 60 ft, producing prose like "you finish 60 ft from the hole (Tour ~18 ft)". 60 ft is a lag-putt distance, physically implausible as an approach-proximity outcome — a coach reading it would diagnose a catastrophic distance-control leak that does not exist, and it lands squarely in the "dial-in / when you do reach it" sentence the recent reach-vs-dial-in redesign was built to keep clean. This is exactly the "ft when you do" artifact the redesign claims to have killed.

Mitigating factor (correctly noted by auditor): requiresStanding=false (line 110), strokes_impact:0, priority:'low' — so the bug does NOT poison a counterfactual stroke value or a StandingBar; it corrupts a displayed diagnostic number only. The proposed fix (treat non-'yards' incl. null as feet — `=== 'yards' ? value*3 : value`) is correct and matches the engine's own normalizeToFeet.

Severity: This is a real, reproducible 3× wrong number a coach reads in production prose (misleading/materially-degraded insight per the high bar), but it is gated to null-unit rows and does not produce a wrong actionable stroke/counterfactual claim a player acts on (which would be critical). The auditor's 'medium' is defensible; I lean 'high' because the inflation is a flagrant 3× producing an absurd distance-control verdict directly in user-facing copy, while the engine already ships a correct normalizer it inconsistently bypasses.

CONFIRMED facts:

confirmedFindings.title: Composite strokes_impact values mix per-round and per-90-day-count units, skewing the flat-feed ranker
confirmedFindings.evidence: doubles-after-bogey: `strokes_impact: compounded * 0.5` where `compounded` is a COUNT of compounded holes over the 90-day window (doubles-after-bogey.ts compose reads match.signals.compounded). closing-hole-fatigue: `strokes_impact: delta * 6` where delta is strokes-PER-HOLE → a per-round value. These two are then compared directly in rankScore (insight-delivery.ts:966) `Math.abs(strokes_impact) × confidence`.
confirmedFindings.impact: A 90-day count (e.g. 8 compounded holes × 0.5 = 4.0) is dimensionally a per-window total, while delta*6 (e.g. 0.5×6 = 3.0) is per-round. They are summed/compared as if identical units, so doubles_after_bogey systematically out-ranks per-round composites and Tier-1 insights purely because a window-count is a bigger raw number. A coach is shown 'doubles after bogey' as the #1 issue even when a per-round leak is larger.
confirmedFindings.fix: Normalize all composite strokes_impact to strokes-per-round before storing: divide count-based impacts by the number of rounds in the window. Document the unit on the field and add a unit assertion/test so future rules can't mix scales.

verdicts.reasoning:
CODE-REPRODUCTION lens: confirmed all four cited file:line snippets exactly. doubles-after-bogey.ts:87 `strokes_impact: compounded * 0.5` where `compounded` (line 43, `if (next.score >= next.par + 2) compounded += 1;`) is incremented per compound event across ALL rounds in the 90-day window — a window-total COUNT, not per-round. By contrast closing-hole-fatigue.ts:87 `strokes_impact: delta * 6` uses delta = per-hole strokes (line 44 `const delta = lateAvg - earlyAvg`) × 6 holes = a per-round stroke value; front-9-starter.ts:87 `delta * 3` is likewise per-round; pressure-decel-chain.ts:75 `strokes_impact: pressureDelta` is a per-round strokes magnitude. So the dimensional mismatch (window-count vs per-round) is real and reproducible.

LIVE PATH: all four rules are registered in COMPOSITE_RULES (composite/index.ts), so synthesis.ts:113 composes and persists them via upsertInsightV3. The ranker rankScore (insight-delivery.ts:965-969, `Math.abs(Number(insight.evidence.strokes_impact ?? 0)) * confidence`) is called at lines 244, 515, 570 and returns ranked[0] as the single top/takeaway insight for getTopInsightForPlayer, getRoundTakeawayInsight. Those feed live UI consumers: CoachHelm dashboard (coachhelm/page.tsx), Round Review (RoundTakeaway.tsx), Player Hub (HubInsightSignalCard.tsx). A second ranking path (insights.ts:2570-2591, W36 rankInsights via ranking/score.ts:80) also reads evidence.strokes_impact directly. The coach-morning-digest cron (scheduled in vercel.json:58) re-ranks (route.ts:363-365) AND renders the raw strokes_impact value in the coach email (route.ts:389), so a window-count like 8*0.5=4.0 is shown to a coach as a per-round stroke figure next to genuine per-round composites. Not dead/v2-orphaned, not flag-gated.

AMPLIFICATION: v3 Tier-1 generators write evidence.strokes_impact = 0 (generator-base.ts:129-142 spreads composed.evidence which keeps the literal `strokes_impact: 0` placeholder seen in every generator e.g. putt-distance.ts:138) and store the real per-round counterfactual under the SEPARATE field evidence.counterfactual.strokes_saved_per_round. So in the flat rankScore/digest paths Tier-1 insights score ~0 and are systematically outranked by any composite carrying nonzero strokes_impact — making the finding's "doubles_after_bogey out-ranks Tier-1 insights" outcome even more true than stated (for an additional reason: Tier-1 impact is literally 0 in these paths). The composite-vs-composite unit mixing is exactly as the finding describes.

Severity: high is correct. It both skews the ranker AND surfaces a 90-day count to a coach as a per-round 'saves ~X strokes' value in the digest — misleading and a degraded/wrong displayed number a coach acts on. Not critical because it is a ranking/labeling distortion rather than a single authoritative wrong number on a primary shot metric. Confidence high — every link reproduced from code.

CONFIRMED as a real dimensional bug, but I am downgrading severity from the claimed "high" to "medium" based on what actually runs and reaches users.

WHAT IS TRUE (verified):
- doubles-after-bogey.ts:87 `strokes_impact: compounded * 0.5` — `compounded` is a COUNT of compounded holes across the entire 90-day window (detect() lines 36-45 accumulate across all rounds; signals.compounded is that raw count). With the ≥20% threshold over typical samples this lands around 3-5; e.g. 8 compounded holes → 4.0. Dimensionally this is a per-90-day-window TOTAL.
- closing-hole-fatigue.ts:87 `strokes_impact: delta * 6` and front-9-starter.ts:87 `delta * 3` — `delta` is strokes-PER-HOLE (computed lateAvg-earlyAvg of score-to-par per hole), so ×6 / ×3 yields a genuine PER-ROUND value (~3.0 / ~1.5).
- pressure-decel-chain.ts:75 `strokes_impact: pressureDelta` — pressureDelta is a per-round tournament-vs-practice scoring delta, also per-round.
- These are compared directly in rankScore (insight-delivery.ts:966 `Math.abs(strokes_impact) × confidence`). synthesis.ts:114-129 writes the raw evidence verbatim with no normalization. So doubles-after-bogey's window-total (4.0) competes against per-round values (3.0, 1.5, 0.5) as if same units, systematically inflating its rank. Domain doc line 306 confirms the per-event 0.5 figure is sane, which makes the bug specifically the count-vs-per-round mixing, not the coefficient.

WHY MEDIUM, NOT HIGH (this is where the finding overstates impact):
1. The PRIMARY v3 read/assemble path is the THEME path (assemble.ts), and it ranks causes by `counterfactual.strokes_saved_per_round` (assemble.ts:280, 403-411) — a clean per-round value — using `|strokes_impact|` ONLY as a secondary tiebreak (assemble.ts:270). The design doc explicitly mandates this: docs/fairway-coachhelm-insight-rebuild.md:23,28 "Causes ranked by counterfactual.strokes_saved (NOT the frequently-zero strokes_impact)." So in the headline theme-card UI, the unit mismatch is a tiebreak-level effect at most.
2. The rankScore flat ranker affects only the LEGACY flat surfaces: getTopInsightForPlayer (Hub top card), getRoundTakeawayInsight, and rankInsights (insights.ts:2580). Crucially, doubles_after_bogey and pressure_decel_chain are priority:'urgent', and getTopInsightForPlayer short-circuits on urgent rows (insight-delivery.ts:198-216) BEFORE rankScore runs — so the Hub top card is not decided by these strokes_impact values among urgent peers.
3. getInsightsForPlayer — the main full feed — orders by created_at DESC (insight-delivery.ts:305), NOT by rankScore, so the main list is unaffected.
4. The finding's claim that this makes doubles "out-rank Tier-1 insights" is partly mis-stated: Tier-1 generators persist strokes_impact:0 (and often confidence:0), e.g. putt-distance.ts:138,140 → rankScore 0. Their real per-round magnitude lives in evidence.counterfactual, never in strokes_impact. So Tier-1 rows already rank at the floor in rankScore surfaces regardless of units; the dimensional mismatch genuinely distorts composite-vs-composite ordering (doubles unfairly beating the per-round fatigue/pressure composites), not composite-vs-Tier-1.

GOLF-DOMAIN VERDICT: A coach/player can be shown "bogeys turning into doubles" as the standout leak on the round-takeaway / legacy surfaces purely because a 90-day count is a bigger raw number than a genuine per-round closing-hole or pressure leak. That is a real, reproducible mis-prioritization of a coaching signal — not cosmetic. But it does not corrupt a displayed stroke number a user reads off a card (the content strings render the underlying count/rate/delta correctly; only the hidden ranking key is wrong), and it is contained to the legacy rankScore-ordered surfaces, with the primary theme view immune. That places it squarely at medium (correctness-adjacent ranking distortion), not high. The proposed fix (normalize count-based impacts to per-round by dividing by rounds-in-window, plus a documented unit + assertion) is correct and appropriate.

The unit mismatch is real and reproducible, but the severity is inflated. CONFIRMED CORE: doubles-after-bogey.ts:87 `strokes_impact: compounded * 0.5` is dimensionally a per-90-day-window COUNT — `compounded` is incremented once per occurrence across ALL rounds in the window (detect loop lines 36-45 `compounded += 1`), with no division by round count. By contrast closing-hole-fatigue.ts:87 `delta * 6`, front-9-starter.ts:87 `delta * 3`, and pressure-decel-chain.ts:75 `pressureDelta` are per-round figures (delta is strokes/hole × holes-in-one-round; pressureDelta is a scoring-avg delta). No normalization occurs downstream: synthesis.ts:114-118 spreads `composed.evidence` verbatim and upsert-v3.ts never touches strokes_impact. NO GUARD neutralizes it on the flat-feed surfaces: getInsightsForCoach (insight-delivery.ts:450-463) and coach-morning-digest (route.ts:355-366) rank purely by |strokes_impact|×confidence with NO urgent short-circuit (the urgent short-circuit only exists in getTopInsightForPlayer:198-216, not the coach feed/digest). All 4 rules are registered live in COMPOSITE_RULES (index.ts:33-42). No test asserts unit consistency. So a window-count composite (e.g. 8×0.5=4.0) will out-sort a genuinely-larger per-round composite (e.g. 0.5/hole→3.0) on these surfaces. WHY SEVERITY IS INFLATED, NOT HIGH: (1) The finding's headline impact — 'doubles_after_bogey out-ranks Tier-1 insights' — is wrong. Tier-1 generators set `strokes_impact: 0` and `confidence: 0` at compose time (e.g. putt-distance.ts:138-140) and BaseGenerator.run (generator-base.ts:113-143) only injects `counterfactual`/`standing`, never repopulating strokes_impact. So every Tier-1 row scores 0 in these flat rankers and is already sorted below ALL composites irrespective of units; the unit bug is not what beats Tier-1. (2) Only 1 of the 4 cited rules (doubles_after_bogey) is actually off-unit; the other three are per-round and are NOT mixed-unit offenders, so the 'rules mix units' framing overcounts. (3) The primary hierarchical surface (themes assemble.ts:280-281) ranks causes by strokesSavedPerRound (per-round counterfactual) FIRST and only uses |strokes_impact| as a tiebreak, so the main player/theme path is protected. Net: a real correctness-adjacent robustness gap that mis-orders composites against each other on the coach flat feed and morning digest, but the documented mechanism is partly incorrect and the blast radius is one offending rule on two non-primary ordering surfaces — medium, not high.

confirmedFindings.title: ParType displays delta-vs-par but injects a counterfactual vs PGA, with a 10×/4× per-round multiplier that can produce large strokes-to-gain on an even-par player
confirmedFindings.evidence: Generator shows `vsPar = agg.playerValue - agg.par` and `comparison_value: agg.par` / `comparison_source: 'absolute_target'`. But base class (generator-base.ts:119-126) computes the counterfactual with `pga_value: standing.pga_value` and lookup factor 10 for scoring_par_4 (`scoring_par_4: { stroke_impact_per_unit: 10 }`). For a player averaging 4.0 on par-4s (even par — strong for college), the card shows '+0.00 vs par' (looks fine) while the PGA gap (4.0 − ~3.95) × 10 ≈ 0.5 strokes/round renders as a leak.
confirmedFindings.impact: A coach reads '+0.0 vs par' (neutral/good) next to a PGA-derived 'close this gap → save ~0.5 strokes' line and can conflate the two reference frames. The 10×/4× per-hole-count multipliers also make par-scoring counterfactuals among the largest the engine produces, so even a small PGA gap reads as material.
confirmedFindings.fix: Use a single, explicit baseline in both the displayed delta and the counterfactual (prefer PGA or cohort), and label the displayed comparison and the counterfactual identically. If par must be the displayed reference, suppress or relabel the PGA counterfactual so the two numbers can't be read against different baselines.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced exactly from live code. DISPLAY side: par-type.ts:79 `const vsPar = agg.playerValue - agg.par;`, title built at line 83 as "(+X vs par)", and evidence at lines 101-103 `comparison_value: agg.par` / `comparison_source: 'absolute_target'` — display is par-referenced. COUNTERFACTUAL side: generator-base.ts:116-126 — because METRIC_RENDER_CONFIG['scoring_par_4'] exists (metric-config.ts:70), the base injects a counterfactual built from `pga_value: standing.pga_value` (line 123), not agg.par. compute.ts:54-55 computes gap=player_value-pga_value (lower_better) and line 65 `strokes_saved_per_round = gap * cfg.stroke_impact_per_unit` with stroke_impact_per_unit=10 for scoring_par_4 (lookup-tables.ts:85; par_3/par_5 = 4). A 4.00 player vs ~3.95 PGA gives 0.05*10=0.5, which exceeds the 0.3 suppress threshold (compute.ts:67, types.ts:10) and renders. So one insight carries a par-referenced "+0.00 vs par" display and a PGA-referenced "save ~0.5 strokes" counterfactual — the claimed dual baseline. The 10x/4x multipliers are confirmed and are among the largest direct unit factors in the lookup table.

LIVE PATH CONFIRMED: generateInsightsForTeam (insights.ts:833) -> coachHelmIntelligence.analyzePlayer (orchestrator.ts:183) -> tier1Generators array (line 230) includes new ParTypeGenerator(playerId, 3/4/5).run() (lines 241-243), executed via Promise.allSettled (line 271). insight-delivery.ts surfaces rows with a non-suppressed evidence.counterfactual (lines 798-800) and carries the par-referenced title through (line 808). Not dead code, not behind a disabled flag.

NUANCE (severity, not reproduction): the my-standing page (page.tsx:226,236) feeds BOTH StandingBar and CounterfactualLine the same pga_value and shows no par-vs-par delta, so that specific surface is internally consistent. The two-reference-frame conflation is real on the insight-card surfaces where the par-referenced title/content sits beside the PGA-derived counterfactual. This is a misleading-presentation/correctness-adjacent issue (coach can read two baselines against each other), not a single wrong hard number acted on in isolation — consistent with medium severity. The structural claim is real and verified, but the user-facing impact is overstated for the GOLF-DOMAIN lens.

VERIFIED:
- par-type.ts:79,101-103: generator displays `vsPar = agg.playerValue - agg.par` and sets `comparison_value: agg.par`, `comparison_source: 'absolute_target'` (par as the displayed reference).
- generator-base.ts:124: the injected counterfactual uses `pga_value: standing.pga_value`, and the standing SQL (20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql:4697 `COALESCE(pga.pga_tour_value, pga.pga_p50)`) confirms `pga_value` is the raw PGA Tour value, not a college cohort. PGA par-4 = 3.97 (pre_20260527/...pga_standards_seed.sql:163-166).
- lookup-tables.ts:85: `scoring_par_4: { stroke_impact_per_unit: 10 }`. So the displayed delta (vs par=4.0) and the counterfactual (vs PGA 3.97 × 10) genuinely use two different baselines. This is exactly the context the domain doc warns against: docs/v3-research-golf-domain.md:349 "Baselines must be context-aware — college baselines (~73 scoring avg) not Tour baselines for player comparison."

MATH CHECK (finding overstates): a player at exactly 4.00 on par-4s → gap = 4.00 - 3.97 = 0.03 → 0.03 × 10 = 0.3 strokes/round, which sits exactly at the suppress boundary (compute.ts:67 suppresses only when `< 0.3`, so 0.3 renders). The finding's "≈0.5 strokes" is wrong for an even-par player; you'd need ~4.02 to reach 0.5. Direction is right, magnitude example is inflated.

WHY UNCERTAIN / IMPACT OVERSTATED:
1. The "+0.0 vs par" string lives only in the par-type insight TITLE/content. The StandingBar shows "delta vs team" (StandingBar/Card.tsx:67), not "vs par". So the StandingBar does not co-render "+0.0 vs par".
2. The raw PGA-derived strokes-saved value renders directly ONLY via CounterfactualLine, which appears only on the LEGACY my-standing path (my-standing/page.tsx:232-240). With NEXT_PUBLIC_REDESIGN=true (set in .env.local:45 and live in prod per memory project_helmv3_prod_serves_foundation), that page takes the Fairway fork (lines 109-170) using StandingStrip with NO CounterfactualLine — so on the live surface the PGA counterfactual line is not shown there at all, and certainly not next to the "+0.0 vs par" title.
3. In the primary v3 THEME cascade, the displayed strokes number is `realisticTeamGap(tourGap, standing)` (assemble.ts:447-448, 108-125), which discounts the raw PGA gap to the team-anchored fraction and clamps to 0 when the player is at/above team avg. So "PGA gap × 10" does not surface raw on theme cards either; the raw value is retained only as the honestly-labeled `tourGapPerRound` "to Tour ceiling".

So the underlying observation (par displayed-delta vs PGA counterfactual; 10×/4× multiplier makes par counterfactuals large) is a genuine, code-confirmed design seam consistent with a documented domain principle. But the concrete "coach reads +0.0 vs par next to a save-0.5-strokes line on the same card" impact does not cleanly occur on the live redesign-on surface, and the magnitude figure is inflated. This is a correctness-adjacent design/labeling concern worth fixing (single explicit baseline, cohort not Tour) but it does not currently produce a wrong number a user acts on side-by-side on the live path. Net: real seam, weaker-than-claimed user-facing impact → medium is slightly high; low is the honest rating.

VERIFIED LIVE & MECHANICALLY REAL, BUT OVERSTATED. The core mechanism checks out: ParTypeGenerator runs on the live path (orchestrator.ts:241-243 inside tier1Generators, reached via analyzePlayer ← insights.ts W25 cutover). `scoring_par_4` IS in METRIC_RENDER_CONFIG (metric-config.ts:70, direction 'lower_better'), so generator-base.ts:116-126 computes the counterfactual with `pga_value: standing.pga_value`. composeContent sets the title to "+X vs par" with comparison_value=agg.par / comparison_source='absolute_target' (par-type.ts:79-103). lookup-tables.ts:84-86 does set factors 4/10/4. So two reference frames (vs-par display vs vs-PGA counterfactual) do coexist on a par-scoring insight. That part is confirmed factual.

WHAT KILLS THE STATED SEVERITY:
1) Magnitude is inflated. The finding assumes PGA par-4 ≈ 3.95 → 0.5 strokes/rd. The actual seeded value is 3.97 (pga_standards_seed.sql:163-166; refresh fn uses pga_value=COALESCE(pga_tour_value,pga_p50)). At even par (4.00): gap=0.03, strokes_saved=0.03×10=EXACTLY 0.3, which sits precisely on COUNTERFACTUAL_SUPPRESS_THRESHOLD (types.ts:10; compute.ts:67 suppresses only when `< 0.3`). So at even par it is the SMALLEST non-suppressed value the engine emits, not "material." To reach 0.5 the player must be ~4.02 (over par), at which point the card reads "+0.02 vs par" — no longer "neutral/good," so the worst-case "neutral card + big leak" is self-limiting.

2) The juxtaposition is mitigated on every primary surface I could trace:
   - /dashboard/my-standing (the surface that actually renders CounterfactualLine): shows the raw par-4 value vs PGA on a StandingBar + a PGA-anchored CounterfactualLine. NO "vs par" framing appears here at all, so no dual-baseline conflict on this page (my-standing/page.tsx:219-240).
   - EvidencePanel: par-type hardcodes evidence.strokes_impact=0 (par-type.ts:108); the compact view hides the strokes number when 0 (EvidencePanel.tsx:306), and EvidencePanel does not render CounterfactualLine — so the counterfactual never surfaces as a number there.
   - Theme cascade (assemble.ts): the DISPLAYED strokes number is the team-anchored realistic gap (`realisticTeamGap = tourGap × teamFraction`, assemble.ts:108-124), further discounted below the raw 0.3, with the raw value explicitly labeled "to Tour." So even where the "+X vs par" title and a strokes number coexist, the rendered number is not the raw 10× PGA gap the finding portrays.

NET: a genuine label/reference-frame inconsistency (vs-par title alongside a PGA-derived counterfactual on the same metric), but it does not produce a wrong or materially misleading NUMBER a user acts on: the magnitude at even par is the suppression floor, the most direct surface (my-standing) has no dual-baseline, EvidencePanel zeros it, and the theme path discounts and re-labels it. This is polish/consistency, not a high/medium correctness hazard. confirmedFindings.title: Severity (priority) persists only on INSERT — the dedup UPDATE path never re-writes it, so severity goes stale
confirmedFindings.evidence: insertNew writes `priority: input.priority ?? 'medium'` (upsert.ts:315), but BOTH branches of updateExisting build update payloads that omit priority entirely: the small-wiggle refresh updates only {evidence, content, title, category, metadata, updated_at} (upsert.ts:186-196) and the >5%-movement path updates {evidence, content, title, category, metadata, updated_at, (lifecycle_state)} (upsert.ts:233-243). The type even documents this: 'The existing-row UPDATE path never writes it' (types.ts:156-157). Re-runs within the 30-day dedup window hit updateExisting, so a row created as priority='high' (e.g. CourseMgmt penalty>0.6, course-mgmt.ts:104) stays 'high' after the player improves to a 'low' value, and vice-versa. The read path orders/filters by the DB priority column directly (insight-delivery.ts:205 `.eq('priority','urgent')`, :428 `.in('priority', opts.priorities)`, :815 reads row.priority) and the DB default is 'medium' (migration 20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql:9059).
confirmedFindings.impact: A coach's alerts surface and urgent-first ordering reflect the severity from the insight's first detection, not its current state. An insight that escalated to 'high' weeks ago keeps shouting 'high' after the player fixed it (until the row falls out of the 30-day window and re-inserts); a newly-worsening insight that was first seen as 'low' stays low-priority and gets buried.
confirmedFindings.fix: In updateExisting add `priority: input.priority` to both update payloads when input.priority is provided (single-metric generators pass ComposedContent.priority, composites pass rule.priority). Guard with `if (input.priority) payload.priority = input.priority` to preserve any coach/triage intent the comment worries about — but generators recompute priority from the latest value every run, so refreshing it is the correct behavior.

But it materially misleads the triage/ordering signal the engine exists to provide: a penalty-rate insight that improved from 0.7→0.2 (high→should be low) keeps the 'high'/'urgent' badge, stays atop the player's feed, sorts above genuinely-urgent issues on the coach dashboard, and inflates "high-priority alert" counts; conversely a worsening insight first seen as 'low' stays buried. confirmedFindings.title: Sand-save insight fires off rounds_played, not sand attempts; sample_n masks the true tiny sample
confirmedFindings.evidence: minSampleN is on rounds: `readonly minSampleN = 5; // rounds_played` (scrambling.ts:40) and aggregate returns `sampleN: roundsPlayed` (scrambling.ts:73). The only attempts guard is `if (data.sand_save_percentage === null) return null` (scrambling.ts:65) — a player with 5+ rounds and just 1-2 sand attempts (non-null sand_save_percentage = e.g. 0% off one bunker) passes the gate and emits 'Sand save rate: 0%'. confirmedFindings.title: getRoundTakeawayInsight primary 'related_round_ids' tagged match can never hit — no generator/composite ever writes that metadata key
confirmedFindings.evidence: .contains('metadata', { related_round_ids: [roundId] })  — a repo-wide search for 'related_round_ids' shows the only writers/readers are insight-delivery.ts itself and its test; no v3 generator, composite synthesis, or upsert-v3 ever stamps metadata.related_round_ids. So strategy 1 always returns 0 rows and the function silently falls through to the strategy-2 temporal updated_at±24h window for every real round.
confirmedFindings.impact: The round-review takeaway never benefits from precise round-level provenance; it always uses the approximate updated_at-within-24h heuristic, which can attach an insight that was last touched (e.g. by a nightly standing refresh) near the round date but is unrelated to that round, and can miss the genuinely round-specific insight if it was written outside the 24h window. Coach/player reads a 'takeaway from this round' that isn't from this round.
confirmedFindings.fix: Either have the engine stamp metadata.related_round_ids on round-triggered insights (then the path works), or delete the dead branch and document the temporal fallback as the only strategy so the contract matches reality.

confirmedFindings.title: EvidenceInsight.player_feedback is declared (and documented as present on player fetchers) but INSIGHT_SELECT never fetches it and neither mapper sets it — always undefined
confirmedFindings.evidence: player_feedback?: InsightPlayerFeedback | null;  with a doc comment 'only present on getInsightsForPlayer / getTopInsightForPlayer'. But INSIGHT_SELECT (lines 153-164) selects no feedback relation, and neither mapRowToEvidenceInsight (896-930) nor mapRowLoose (789-822) ever assigns player_feedback. confirmedFindings.impact: Any consumer that branches on insight.player_feedback (e.g. to hide an already-dismissed/acknowledged card or show a 'you marked this helpful' state) silently gets undefined and renders the default state — a player who dismissed/rated an insight sees no reflection of that. Misleading API contract vs runtime.
confirmedFindings.fix: Either join the feedback row into INSIGHT_SELECT for the player fetchers and populate player_feedback, or remove the field + its doc claim so the contract matches what's returned.

confirmedFindings.title: getInsightsForCoach over-fetches only min(50, limit×4) ordered by created_at then ranks-by-zero — combined with the zero-rank bug, high-value older insights past the cap are never seen
confirmedFindings.evidence: const PRE_RANK_FETCH = Math.min(50, limit * 4); ... .order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(PRE_RANK_FETCH);  — the comment says 'Pull a wider set so the in-app rank-and-cut has room to favor impact + confidence over recency', but because the rank key is |strokes_impact|×confidence = 0 (see coach-feed-ranks-by-zero finding), the 'wider set' is just the newest PRE_RANK_FETCH rows and the rank-and-cut cannot favor impact.
confirmedFindings.impact: A genuinely high-counterfactual insight older than the newest ~PRE_RANK_FETCH rows is never even fetched, so it cannot be ranked up. The default coach feed (limit 20 → fetch 50) silently truncates to the 50 newest and then can't reorder them by value — the most actionable insight on a busy roster can be invisible.
confirmedFindings.fix: Once ranking is counterfactual-based, either compute the counterfactual in-DB and order by it before the cap, or raise/justify the pre-rank cap; at minimum order the pre-rank fetch by something correlated with value (priority then created_at) rather than created_at alone so the cap doesn't pre-discard high-value rows.

confirmedFindings.evidence: compose() prose: `When bunker shots leak ${dir}-of-pin and your putts tend to miss ${dir}, you're effectively short-siding yourself twice`. confirmedFindings.fix: Drop the side-equivalence claim. Either gate on a genuine bunker leave-side signal, or reframe as two independent short-game leaks without asserting they share a side.

confirmedFindings.title: practice_tournament_delta counterfactual projects the entire pressure gap as recoverable strokes (factor 1.0)
confirmedFindings.evidence: `practice_tournament_delta: { stroke_impact_per_unit: 1.0, coachable_timeframe_weeks: 16 }`. compute.ts:65 multiplies the gap (competitive_avg - practice_avg, after subtracting the 0.5 Tour reference) by 1.0, i.e. assumes the full tournament-vs-practice gap above Tour is closable strokes. confirmedFindings.impact: A college player with a typical 2-5 stroke practice-to-tournament gap (doc-normal) gets a counterfactual claiming nearly the whole gap can be erased, the largest single strokes-saved number in the feed, over-prioritising pressure work and setting an unrealistic target.

DOMAIN JUDGMENT — the finding is real but partially mis-diagnosed. Domain doc §9/§10 (lines 300, 329, 342) is explicit: pressure gaps are college-typical 2-5 strokes, pressure performance is only 'moderately coachable... simulation training works but slow', and mental skills 'lag physical ones... indefinitely without competitive reps.' I verified the full live chain. The mechanical facts in the finding are correct: lookup-tables.ts:92 sets `practice_tournament_delta: { stroke_impact_per_unit: 1.0, coachable_timeframe_weeks: 16 }`; PressureGapGenerator (pressure-gap.ts:44) uses metricId `practice_tournament_delta`, inherits the default `requiresStanding=true` (generator-base.ts:59), and the metric is present in METRIC_RENDER_CONFIG (metric-config.ts:77, direction `lower_better`), so generator-base.ts:126 DOES call computeCounterfactual on the live generation path. The standing's pga_value comes from golf_pga_standards where the seed for this metric is 0.5 (seed line 186; RPC writes COALESCE(pga_tour_value,pga_p50) at baseline.sql:4808). So compute.ts:55 yields gap = (competitive_avg − practice_avg) − 0.5 and compute.ts:65 multiplies by 1.0 — exactly as the finding claims. The domain doc corroborates that pressure is only "Moderately Coachable (Months-to-Years)", "simulation training works but slow", players "plateau on pressure putting", and mental skills lag "indefinitely without competitive reps" — so a 1.0 closable factor over 16 weeks is optimistic and at odds with the doc.

BUT the skeptic lens kills the severity claim, not the existence of the issue. The finding's central impact — "claiming nearly the whole gap can be erased, the largest single strokes-saved number in the feed" — is materially neutralized on the live READ/DISPLAY path. The raw 1.0-factor counterfactual is carried only as `tourGapPerRound` (assemble.ts:447/tourGapOf). The PRIMARY number that is ranked, sized, and rendered to the user is `strokesSavedPerRound = realisticTeamGap(tourGap, standing)` (assemble.ts:448/501), which equals tourGap × clamp01((player_value − team_avg)/(player_value − pga_value)) — i.e. the gap to the player's OWN TEAM AVERAGE, a strictly smaller number. CauseRow.tsx:145-151,173-177 shows this as "≈X/rd to team avg", with the raw Tour gap appearing only as a secondary, honestly-labeled "(X to Tour)" ceiling note. The raw 1.0 number becomes the primary displayed value only in the no-team-reference fallback (team_avg null, e.g. solo/small roster), where realisticTeamGap returns the full tourGap labeled "to Tour". So the alarming over-claim survives only in an edge case, and even there it is framed as a ceiling, not a promise.

Net: the finding is real (a 1.0 closability factor and 16wk horizon for an admittedly slow/partial skill is a modeling imperfection that contradicts the domain doc) but the claimed medium severity is inflated — it does not produce the prominent "largest strokes-saved" actionable number on the normal path because of the team-anchoring clamp; it is correctness-adjacent / polish-level, surfaced as an honest "to Tour ceiling" secondary number in the dominant case. Confidence in the mechanics is high; confidence that the user-facing impact is small (not medium) is also high given the verified clamp.

confirmedFindings.title: Composites print green-hit pct as feet
confirmedFindings.evidence: prints your_value (green-hit pct, approach-miss 194) as ft.
confirmedFindings.impact: Absurd percent-as-feet next to Tour 18 ft.
confirmedFindings.fix: Use proximity_when_hit feet.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced exactly from code on the LIVE v3 path.

WIRING (live): generateInsightsForTeam (src/app/golf/actions/insights.ts:833) -> coachHelmIntelligence.analyzePlayer -> orchestrator runs ApproachMissGenerator as Tier-1 (src/lib/coachhelm/v2/orchestrator.ts:252-254) then synthesizeForPlayer (orchestrator.ts:307). synthesizeForPlayer (src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/synthesis.ts:76,113) iterates COMPOSITE_RULES, which include shortApproachGap and longApproach3Putt (src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/index.ts:37-38). Not dead, not flag-gated.

ROOT DATA SHAPE: After the reach-vs-dial-in redesign, ApproachMissGenerator emits, in evidence, your_value = green_hit_pct with unit 'percent' (src/lib/coachhelm/v3/generators/approach-miss.ts:193-196), signature `approach_miss:{bucket}` (line 189). The real proximity lives only on the aggregate field proximity_when_hit_feet (line 150) and is NEVER written into evidence.

DEFECT (short-approach-proximity-gap.ts): isWeakShortApproach reads `Number(i.evidence.your_value ?? 0)` and gates on `yourVal > 22` (lines 19-20) against an approach_miss whose your_value is a 0-100 green-hit percent; detect copies it into approach_proximity_ft (line 42); compose prints `you're leaving the ball ${proximity} ft from the hole on average (Tour is ~18 ft)` (lines 49,54) and stores unit:'feet', your_value:proximity (lines 64-65). So a player hitting e.g. 60% greens is told "60 ft from the hole (Tour ~18 ft)". The >22 threshold also misfires: an 80%-green striker triggers the "leak" and is told "80 ft".

DEFECT (long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts, cited line 57): isWeakLongApproach reads the 175_plus_ft approach_miss your_value (green-hit percent) with a stale comment "for approach_miss the lower-better unit is feet; >50 ft is weak" (lines 20-21) and threshold >50; compose prints `Your 175+ yd approaches average ${proximity} ft from the hole` (line 57) with comparison 45 ft. Same percent-as-feet error; the comment is left over from the half-done unit fix.

The proposed fix (use proximity_when_hit feet) is correct in intent but cannot be applied as-is because that field is not exposed in evidence today; the generator must also write proximity_when_hit_feet into evidence (and the rules must guard the null case).

Confidence ~0.95. Both cited file:line locations match the offending code precisely.

CONFIRMED, and the real bug is worse than the finding describes. The reach-vs-dial-in redesign repurposed the approach_miss insight's evidence.your_value to be GREEN-HIT PERCENT, not proximity feet. Verified at /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/generators/approach-miss.ts:193-195: `unit: 'percent'` / `your_value: agg.green_hit_pct` / `your_value_display: ghDisp` (ghDisp = `${pct}%`). Both downstream composites still read this as proximity-in-feet:

1) short-approach-proximity-gap.ts:42 `approach_proximity_ft: Number(approach.evidence.your_value ?? 0)` then :54 prints `you're leaving the ball ${proximity} ft from the hole on average (Tour is ~18 ft)`. With your_value being a college green-hit % (~70-80% in the 50-125 yd band per research doc lines 87/254), this renders nonsense like "78 ft from 50-125 yd vs Tour ~18 ft" — a physically absurd proximity no real player has.

2) long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts:45 `approach_proximity_ft: Number(longApproach.evidence.your_value ?? 0)` then :57 prints `Your 175+ yd approaches average ${proximity} ft from the hole`. Here green-hit % (~50% Tour, research doc lines 254/261) coincidentally overlaps real proximity (45 ft), making the wrong number harder to spot but still meaningless.

DEEPER PROBLEM the finding missed: the detection gates are now INVERTED. short-approach-proximity-gap.ts:20 `return yourVal > 22` and long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts:21 `Number(...your_value...) > 50` were written for lower-is-better feet, but your_value is now higher-is-better percent. So these composites fire for GOOD ball-strikers (80% greens > 22; 55% greens > 50) and stay silent for the weak players they exist to flag — wrong audience plus wrong number.

LIVE-PATH CONFIRMED: generateInsightsForTeam (insights.ts) -> v2/orchestrator.ts:307 synthesizeForPlayer -> composite/synthesis.ts (COMPOSITE_RULES) -> both rules imported in composite/index.ts:18,21. The loader (composite/loader.ts:23) reads persisted `evidence` from golf_coach_insights, i.e. the percent your_value the generator wrote. Not dead code.

DOMAIN VERDICT: This genuinely misleads. A coach reading "78 ft from a wedge distance" or building a development plan from these composites is acting on a fabricated number, and the composite surfaces on the wrong player. The proposed fix ("use proximity_when_hit feet") is directionally correct but currently blocked: the generator computes proximity_when_hit_feet on its aggregate (approach-miss.ts:150) but does NOT persist it into the evidence object (the ComposedContent evidence block, lines 190-211, omits it), so the composites can't read it without a generator change first. Note also it's nullable (null when <3 greens hit), which the composites must handle.

NOTE on citations: long-approach is at long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts (line 57), not a "long-approach-proximity-gap.ts" — the finding's filename for #2 was slightly off but the line and substance match. The "194" reference is approach-miss.ts:194, the source of the percent value.

Severity: rubric says critical = "produces a wrong number/claim a user acts on." This does exactly that (absurd ft figure in a coaching development plan) AND inverts targeting. I rate it critical rather than the claimed high, tempered only by the fact that firing is conditional (both source insights must exist and the inverted gate must pass).

I tried to kill this finding and could not — the unit-mismatch is real, on the live path, with no guard. Trace:

GENERATOR writes a percent, not feet. /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/generators/approach-miss.ts:193-195 sets `unit: 'percent'`, `your_value: agg.green_hit_pct`, `your_value_display: ghDisp` (e.g. "60%"). The recent unit-inflation fix deliberately moved your_value OFF proximity-feet ONTO green-hit pct (comment lines 21-26, 132-133). Proximity now lives in a separate field `proximity_when_hit_feet` (line 101/150) — exactly the field the finding proposes using.

LOADER is a pure pass-through. /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/loader.ts:22-37 selects `evidence` straight from golf_coach_insights with no transformation; the percent reaches the composites verbatim.

COMPOSITE reads that percent and prints it as feet. /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/rules/short-approach-proximity-gap.ts:19-20 `const yourVal = Number(i.evidence.your_value ?? 0); return yourVal > 22;` treats the green-hit percent as a feet threshold; line 42 copies it to `approach_proximity_ft`; lines 49,54,65 render `${proximity} ft ... (Tour is ~18 ft)`. So a player hitting 60% of greens prints "leaving the ball 60 ft from the hole on average (Tour is ~18 ft)". Absurd percent-as-feet next to Tour 18 ft — exactly as claimed. The fix (use proximity_when_hit feet) is correct.

SYNTHESIS provides no guard. /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/synthesis.ts:113 just calls rule.compose(match); nothing reinterprets the unit. shortApproachGap is wired live in /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/index.ts:38.

SKEPTIC checks that FAILED to kill it: (1) It does NOT silently never-fire — the detection threshold is in fact inverted: `green_hit_pct > 22` is true for nearly anyone who reaches greens, so the "weak short approach" gate trips for GOOD ball-strikers; the only real gate is the co-occurring weak-scrambling insight (team_pct < 40), which is common. The real long-band rule is /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/rules/long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts, which carries the IDENTICAL defect: line 21 `Number(i.evidence.your_value ?? 0) > 50` (percent>50 read as feet), line 45 copies to approach_proximity_ft, line 57 prints `Your 175+ yd approaches average ${proximity} ft from the hole`. So the mechanism is confirmed in BOTH composite rules; the finding just mis-named the second file.

Severity: the claimed `high` is right and arguably conservative. When fired it states a flatly wrong proximity number a coach/player would act on, juxtaposed with a Tour anchor that makes it look catastrophic — close to critical by the wrong-number-user-acts-on rule.
