confirmedFindings.title: Hero ignores citation verifier
confirmedFindings.evidence: verifyCitations only logged; raw text returned; card no check.
confirmedFindings.impact: Hallucinated hero number shown.
confirmedFindings.fix: Fallback when unverified.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced exactly as described, on the live path.

compose.ts:147 computes `const verification = verifyCitations(text, req.evidence);`. The verifier result is consumed only by the call-log INSERT (lines 160-161: `citations: { unmatched_tokens: verification.unmatched_tokens }, verified: verification.verified`). The return block at compose.ts:173-179 returns `{ text, used_llm: true, citations_verified: verification.verified, ... }` — line 174 `text,` is the RAW LLM output, returned unconditionally. There is no branch that substitutes `fallbackText` when `verification.verified === false`. So an unverified (potentially fabricated) number is returned to callers as the primary text, with verification demoted to a sibling boolean.

The consumer chain confirms the boolean is then dropped: generateHeroNarrative (v3/llm.ts:222-228) returns `text: result.text` and passes `citations_verified` along but never gates on it; HeroNarrativeCard.tsx:65-67 renders with the only check being `if (r.ok && r.text) { setText(r.text); setUsedLlm(!!r.used_llm); }` — `r.citations_verified` is never inspected. Worse, the card displays a "CoachHelm ✦" authority badge (lines 112-127) keyed off `used_llm`, lending credibility to prose that may have failed verification.

Live-path verification: HeroNarrativeCard is mounted on the production player dashboard (PlayerCoachHelmDashboard.tsx:382) and FairwayPlayerCoachHelm.tsx. The LLM call is reachable whenever checkBudget (budget.ts:64, `allowed = budget_usd > 0 && remaining >= estimated_cost_usd`) passes, which the W30 prereqs (settings.llm_budget>0, llm_narrative_enabled=true) describe as an enabled production config. This is not dead/v2 code.

Severity nuance keeping it at medium rather than high: verifyCitations is a conservative extractor (citations.ts:22-52) with a SAFE-list (0,1,2,3,100) and unit-normalization, so it catches only some fabricated numbers and tolerates false positives by design; the hero prompt is tightly grounded and registers displayed values as evidence (hero-narrative.ts:89-111), so a flagged hallucination reaching the user is a real but bounded, non-guaranteed event. The architectural defect — a verifier whose verdict is computed then ignored at both the wrapper return and the card render — is exactly the claimed issue. The proposed fix (fall back when unverified) is the correct direction.

Confirmed on the live path. compose.ts:147 runs verifyCitations(); compose.ts:173-176 returns the raw `text` unconditionally (line 174 `text,`) with `citations_verified: verification.verified` as a flag but NO fallback substitution when verified===false. The flag propagates through generateHeroNarrative (src/app/golf/actions/v3/llm.ts:226 `citations_verified: result.citations_verified`) all the way to the action result. But HeroNarrativeCard.tsx:65-68 (`if (r.ok && r.text) { setText(r.text); setUsedLlm(!!r.used_llm); }`) reads r.text and r.used_llm and NEVER reads r.citations_verified. So an unverified hero paragraph is rendered to the player regardless. The card is live: used at PlayerCoachHelmDashboard.tsx:382 and FairwayPlayerCoachHelm.tsx:92.

The finding's localization (line 174) is accurate; its evidence wording "verifyCitations only logged" is slightly off (the flag is also returned, not only logged), but the load-bearing claim — raw text returned, card does no check, hallucinated hero number shown — is fully verified.

GOLF-DOMAIN judgment: this is a genuine, non-cosmetic harm. The hero prompt (hero-narrative.ts:74-76) instructs the model to surface exactly one action-driving number: team percentile, goal target, or counterfactual stroke-savings. These are precisely the numbers a player/coach acts on for practice prioritization. A hallucinated stroke-savings ("worth ~2 strokes/round") or wrong percentile is exactly the failure class the verifier exists to catch (citations.ts:6-7, citing master-plan Part XI.3). The verifier correctly detects it (verified=false) and the signal reaches the UI boundary, then is silently dropped — defeating the grounding discipline.

Severity: the harness defines critical as "produces a wrong number/claim a user acts on." A hallucinated hero number qualifies. But the realistic frequency is bounded — a tightly grounded prompt with an explicit "do NOT invent any number" instruction hallucinates infrequently, and the verifier already detects the case; only the UI fallback is missing. This is a wired-but-disconnected defense-in-depth gap, not a deterministic always-wrong computation, so it sits at the high end of high rather than guaranteed-critical. The claimed `medium` understates it: an existing verification signal is deliberately ignored at render time. Confidence high (~0.9) on the code chain; the "shown to user" impact is confirmed, the open variable is only how often the LLM actually fabricates.

The finding is code-accurate but its impact is overstated. SKEPTIC verification:

REAL part (confirmed): /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/lib/coachhelm/v3/llm/compose.ts:147 computes `const verification = verifyCitations(text, req.evidence)` then at lines 173-179 returns the raw model `text` with `citations_verified: verification.verified` (line 176) but NO fallback/suppression when unverified. No consumer gates on the flag: the action src/app/golf/actions/v3/llm.ts:224-226 merely passes it through, and the live card src/components/golf/coachhelm/v3/HeroNarrativeCard.tsx:65-67 does `if (r.ok && r.text) { setText(r.text); setUsedLlm(!!r.used_llm); }` — `citations_verified` is never read. This IS the live path (mounted in PlayerCoachHelmDashboard.tsx:382 and FairwayPlayerCoachHelm.tsx:886). So an LLM paragraph with a fabricated number does render. The finding's evidence ("verifyCitations only logged; raw text returned; card no check") is correct.

WHY SEVERITY IS INFLATED (the kill attempt, partially successful):
1. The load-bearing "hero number" the user acts on is NOT produced by the LLM. The grounded metric (your_value_display, team_pct, counterfactual) is computed deterministically upstream and is the headline shown by the dashboard/HeroInsightCard. It is passed INTO the LLM as fixed evidence (hero-narrative.ts:89-111) and the prompt pins the headline to it (hero-narrative.ts:74-77, "do NOT invent any number"). The HeroNarrativeCard is a 2-3 sentence flavor paragraph sitting ABOVE the real number card. The finding's impact "Hallucinated hero number shown" misframes a flavor-prose risk as a corruption of the primary number — the primary number stays correct regardless of verification.
2. The verifier only catches EXTRA numbers injected into prose (e.g. the test case "takes about 5 weeks", hero-narrative.test.ts:60-72). Worst case is a misleading secondary number in an obviously-AI paragraph (badged "CoachHelm" / ✦), not a wrong primary stat a user acts on.
3. This is a documented, deliberate design, not an oversight: src/lib/coachhelm/v3/llm/types.ts:54-55 — "False = at least one fabricated cite — caller decides whether to surface anyway." The verifier is advisory by design; ignoring it is a robustness gap, not a correctness bug.

Net: the mechanism is real and on the live path, so not refuted, but the claimed medium overstates it. A hallucinated secondary number in an advisory flavor paragraph, with the grounded headline protected by the deterministic upstream card, is a low-severity robustness gap (correctness-adjacent metadata not acted on), not a number/claim a user acts on. Per the lens instruction, real-but-overstated → suggest lower severity.

confirmedFindings.title: Tone calls lower-is-better encouraging
confirmedFindings.evidence: scoring_par, delta, big_number_rate miss negative regex.
confirmedFindings.impact: Worse results read as encouraging.
confirmedFindings.fix: Add to negative polarity.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced the finding directly from code. At src/components/golf/coachhelm/insight-card/tone-derivation.ts:56-58 the encouraging branch fires when `your_value > comparison_value && isPositivePolarityMetric(metric)`. Line 75 defines `NEGATIVE_METRIC_PATTERN = /severity|score_to_par|miss|stddev|dispersion|penalty/i`, and isPositivePolarityMetric returns `!isNegativePolarityMetric` (line 83-85), so any metric not matching that regex is treated as more-is-better.

The live v3 engine emits these lower-is-better metric IDs that the regex misses:
- big_number_rate — metric-config.ts:66 direction 'lower_better'; emitted by course-mgmt.ts (VARIANT_TO_METRIC_ID big_number:'big_number_rate', line 27; metric: this.metricId line 144). Does NOT match the regex (no "penalty"/"miss"/etc).
- scoring_par_3/4/5 — metric-config.ts:69-71 'lower_better'; emitted by par-type.ts (PAR_TO_METRIC_ID, metric: this.metricId line 96). The regex has 'score_to_par' (underscores) which does not match the literal 'scoring_par_*' strings.
- practice_tournament_delta (pressure-gap.ts:44,119) and opening_hole_delta (warmup-hole.ts:34,122) — metric-config.ts:77-78 'lower_better'; regex has no 'delta'.

Consequence: a player whose your_value exceeds the comparison on any of these (i.e., MORE double-bogeys, HIGHER par-scoring, LARGER pressure/opening-hole gap = worse) gets isPositivePolarityMetric=true and the card renders 'encouraging'. Worse results read as encouraging — exactly the claimed impact.

LIVE-path confirmation: evidence.metric is populated from the canonical metric_id by every generator (metric: this.metricId). deriveTone is consumed by InsightCard.tsx:232 and round-review/RoundTakeaway.tsx:79; the insight-card InsightCard is imported by player-hub HubInsightSignalCard, stats StatsIntelligenceStrip, and fairway FairwayPlayerInsight — all user-facing. Not dead/v2 code, no disabling flag.

Severity nuance (supports claimed medium, not higher): the encouraging branch is reachable only after the earlier cautionary gates (priority==='high' at line 50, and Math.abs(strokesImpact)*confidence>1.0 at line 51) fail to fire, so the mispaint is confined to lower-impact/lower-confidence rows. It is a misleading visual-tone bug, not a wrong stroke number — so high (misleading insight) to medium is the right band. The existing test InsightCard.test.tsx:147-158 and 181-186 never exercise the real v3 metric IDs (uses generic/legacy names like miss_severity, score_to_par), so the gap is genuinely unguarded. Finding confirmed; proposed fix (add these to negative polarity) is correct.

CONFIRMED and live. tone-derivation.ts:75 NEGATIVE_METRIC_PATTERN = /severity|score_to_par|miss|stddev|dispersion|penalty/i drives isPositivePolarityMetric() (line 83-85), used at line 58: `if (yourAhead && isPositivePolarityMetric(metric)) return 'encouraging'`. yourAhead is `your_value > comparison_value` (line 57). For a lower-better metric, your_value > comparison_value means the player is WORSE than the benchmark, yet the metric falls through to positive polarity, so a worse-than-comp result is tagged 'encouraging'.

I verified the canonical direction table at src/lib/coachhelm/v3/standing/metric-config.ts: many lower_better metrics miss the regex. Running the regex over the lower_better set, these are mis-classified as positive (BUG): approach_proximity_50_125ft / 125_175ft / 175_plus_ft, big_number_rate, scoring_par_3/4/5, practice_tournament_delta, opening_hole_delta, plus composite-rule lower-better strings (closing_hole_delta, compound_mistake_rate, three_putt_chain, short_side_proximity, flyer_lie_proximity). The regex only catches the *_miss_bias_*, penalty_rate_per_round, and score_to_par/severity families. So the finding under-counts the affected metrics (it lists 3; ~9+ are affected) but the core claim is right.

The path is live and reachable, not just theoretical. evidence.metric carries the v3 metric_id (generators set `metric: this.metricId`; insight-delivery.ts mapRowToEvidenceInsight passes it through to deriveTone). The generators are all wired in src/lib/coachhelm/v2/orchestrator.ts:33-254. ParTypeGenerator (par-type.ts:92-110) emits priority:'low', strokes_impact:0, confidence:0 with your_value=playerValue and comparison_value=agg.par — so a player averaging over par on par-4s satisfies every short-circuit skip (not resolved/urgent/pressure/high; |0|*0<=1.0) and lands on the encouraging branch with yourAhead=true. CourseMgmtGenerator big_number (course-mgmt.ts:131-150) similarly: a 3% double-bogey rate (worse than the PGA ~2% baseline it documents as the '#1 separator between 70s and 80s') gets priority:'medium' (doesn't short-circuit), strokes_impact:0, confidence:0 -> encouraging.

User-facing impact is real, not cosmetic: encouraging renders a green IconTrophy (InsightCard.tsx:172-179, bg-primary-50, text-primary-700) and in round review (RoundTakeaway.tsx:80-83) it is literally labeled "Today's bright spot" with bright:true. A genuine weakness (over-par scoring, above-baseline big-number rate, long approach proximity, pressure/warmup deltas) can be presented to a player/coach as a celebrated strength — a direct inversion of the coaching signal that could cause a player to de-prioritize a real weakness. Partial mitigant: the StandingBar below uses the correct lower_better direction from metric-config, so the true numeric standing is still visible on InsightCard; the RoundTakeaway "bright spot" label, however, has no such numeric guardrail.

Proposed fix direction is correct but incomplete: rather than appending to the regex, isPositivePolarityMetric should consult the canonical METRIC_RENDER_CONFIG direction (lower_better => negative polarity) so it stays in sync with the 28-metric source of truth and covers the composite-rule metric strings too.

CONFIRMED — and the SKEPTIC lens actually strengthened the finding rather than killing it.

Live path: deriveTone() in /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/components/golf/coachhelm/insight-card/tone-derivation.ts runs on two live surfaces — InsightCard.tsx:232 and RoundTakeaway.tsx:79/184. evidence.metric is the canonical v3 metric_id (insight-delivery.ts:908 requires it as a string), so real metric IDs reach the regex.

The bug: NEGATIVE_METRIC_PATTERN = /severity|score_to_par|miss|stddev|dispersion|penalty/i (line 75) misclassifies live lower-is-better metrics as positive-polarity. Verified by executing the regex against the registry: scoring_par_3/4/5, big_number_rate, practice_tournament_delta, opening_hole_delta all return positive — yet METRIC_RENDER_CONFIG (standing/metric-config.ts:69-78) authoritatively marks every one as direction:'lower_better'. The regex's 'score_to_par' token never matches the actual id 'scoring_par_4'. So tone-derivation reimplements polarity with a regex that contradicts the engine's own canonical direction table, which it ignores.

Reachability — no guard exists; the upstream generator GUARANTEES the bad path. ParTypeGenerator (generators/par-type.ts:93,108,110) unconditionally emits a par-scoring insight with hardcoded priority:'low', strokes_impact:0, confidence:0, your_value=playerValue, comparison_value=par. For any college golfer averaging over par on a par type (the norm), your_value>comparison_value is true, the cautionary gate Math.abs(0)*0>1.0 is false, priority isn't high/urgent, and the metric reads as positive — so deriveTone returns 'encouraging'. I reproduced the exact generator output (4.30 avg on par 4): result = 'encouraging'. The penalty_rate control (caught by regex) correctly returns 'neutral', confirming the misclassification is the cause. course-mgmt.ts:141 likewise sets big_number_rate to priority:'low' when value<=2, feeding the same path.

Impact is worse than a color: in RoundTakeaway, buildPreheader (RoundTakeaway.tsx:80-83) maps encouraging -> label "Today's bright spot", bright:true, and sets it as the section aria-label; InsightCard TONE_CONFIG.encouraging (InsightCard.tsx:173-180) paints a trophy icon + green primary styling. So a player who is WORSE than par/team on par-4 scoring, blows up more holes (big_number_rate), or chokes more under tournament pressure (practice_tournament_delta) has that weakness presented as a celebrated bright spot.

Cited file:line (57, 75) are exactly right and evidence is accurate. The proposed fix is valid (better: source polarity from METRIC_RENDER_CONFIG.direction rather than the regex). No test guards the lower-better case (InsightCard.test.tsx only tests a positive metric).

Severity: claimed medium understates it. This is on the live path, is the default (not edge) outcome via the unconditional ParTypeGenerator, and emits a misleading positive textual + iconographic claim on a player weakness = high ('misleading/materially degraded insight'). Not critical because it inverts framing/tone, not a numeric strokes-saved value.

confirmedFindings.title: 30-49yd shots tagged 'approach' at entry are dropped from BOTH approach-proximity and around-the-green stats (boundary mismatch)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Entry tags around_green only at <=30yd: `const distanceInYards = state.distanceUnit === 'feet' ? state.distanceToHole / 3 : state.distanceToHole; if (distanceInYards <= 30) return 'around_green'; return 'approach';`. But the calculator's approach-eff/proximity loop requires distance >= 50 (golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:1782 `hole.approachDistance >= AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS`) and getApproachDistanceBucket returns '' for <50 (line 480), while the ATG-efficiency loop filters strictly to shot_type==='around_green' (golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:1855 `hole.shots.filter(s => s.shot_type === 'around_green')`). A shot from 31-49yd is stored shot_type='approach' (>30) so it is excluded from ATG, and its distance <50 so it is excluded from approach proximity/efficiency buckets.
confirmedFindings.impact: Every wedge/short-iron shot from ~31-49 yards is silently invisible to both the Approach and Around-the-Green proximity/efficiency stats. A player who is weak from 40 yards sees no cause for it in either theme, and approach-proximity counts/averages are understated.
confirmedFindings.fix: Reconcile the boundary to ONE value. Either raise the entry around_green cutoff to 50yd (use-shot-state-machine.ts:866) to match AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS, or change the calculator/shot-source to bucket by stored shot_type only (not a second distance gate). Per spec gap #7, pick one band-edge set and apply it at entry, in the calculator, and in shot-source.bucketApproachDistance.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced the core mechanism, with corrections to the exact claims.

ENTRY (confirmed exactly): src/hooks/golf/use-shot-state-machine.ts:865-867 `const distanceInYards = state.distanceUnit === 'feet' ? state.distanceToHole / 3 : state.distanceToHole; if (distanceInYards <= 30) return 'around_green'; return 'approach';` — a shot from 31-49yd to the hole is stored shot_type='approach'.

CALCULATOR (confirmed, but cited PATH is wrong): the file is src/lib/utils/golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts, NOT src/lib/coachhelm/v2/golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts (that path does not exist). The cited line numbers do match the real file:
- :519 `export const AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS = 50;`
- :480 `if (distance < AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS) return '';` (getApproachDistanceBucket drops <50 from by-distance proximity buckets, used at :1769-1774)
- :1782 approach-EFFICIENCY by-distance gated `hole.approachDistance >= AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS` → 31-49yd dropped
- :1855 `const aroundGreenShots = hole.shots.filter(s => s.shot_type === 'around_green');` → a 31-49yd shot tagged 'approach' is excluded from ATG efficiency.
So a 31-49yd shot is excluded from BOTH approach-by-distance buckets/efficiency AND ATG efficiency — the deadzone is real.

CORRECTIONS to the finding's impact claim: it is OVERSTATED in two ways. (1) Overall approach proximity is NOT understated — :1746 `approachProximities.push(...)` and the par/lie splits :1759-1765 are NOT distance-gated; a 40yd green-hit approach still counts in overall/by-par/by-lie averages. Only the by-DISTANCE bucket (:1769) and by-distance efficiency (:1782) drop it. (2) approachProximity is on-green-only (:839-846), so a 40yd shot contributes proximity only when it hit the green. (3) Scrambling % is NOT affected: the aroundGreenShot finder at :873-883 catches 31-49yd shots via its OR distance<=50 branch, so chip-based scramble stats still count them; only ATG efficiency-by-distance is lost.

LIVE PATH (key for this lens): the cited v2 calculator feeds the stats display surfaces (stats-data.ts:997, player-profile-stats.ts:243) and golf_player_stats_cache — it is NOT imported by the v3 insight generators. BUT the same deadzone independently exists on the v3 insight engine via DIFFERENT code: src/lib/coachhelm/v3/engine/shot-source.ts loadApproachShots (:104 `.eq('shot_type', 'approach')`) loads the 31-49yd shots, then bucketApproachDistance (:69-74 `if (yards >= 50 ...) ... return null`) returns null for yards<50, so the approach-miss generator filter (approach-miss.ts:124) silently drops them — and being tagged 'approach' they appear in no around_green insight. So the band-edge deadzone genuinely reaches the live insight engine, exactly matching the finding's spec gap #7 (entry + calculator + shot-source.bucketApproachDistance all need ONE band edge).

VERDICT: confirmed — the deadzone exists and is on the live path (both v2 stats cache and v3 insights). Caveats: cited file path is wrong (right line numbers), and the impact is narrower than claimed (by-distance approach buckets, by-distance ATG efficiency, and v3 approach insights — not overall proximity averages or scrambling %). Severity: the affected outputs are by-distance breakdowns and the v3 approach insight, a materially degraded/misleading insight rather than a headline wrong number on a primary metric, and overall aggregates remain correct — so high is slightly aggressive; medium is the more defensible calibration, leaning high only because it silently suppresses a real weakness (a player weak from 40yd gets no cause in either theme).

CONFIRMED, with one phrasing correction. The mechanism is real and on the live v3 path.

Boundary mismatch verified:
- Entry: `src/hooks/golf/use-shot-state-machine.ts:866` — `if (distanceInYards <= 30) return 'around_green'; return 'approach';` so a 31-49yd-to-hole shot is stored shot_type='approach'.
- v3 LIVE approach path drops it: `src/lib/coachhelm/v3/engine/shot-source.ts:104` loads `.eq('shot_type','approach')`, then `bucketApproachDistance` (shot-source.ts:69-74) `if (yards >= 50 && yards < 125) ... return null` returns null for <50yd. The v3 registry's lowest approach bucket is `approach_proximity_50_125ft` (registry.ts:41) — there is NO <50yd approach metric at all, and approach-miss.ts:124 filters to `bucketApproachDistance(...) === this.bucket`, so the 31-49yd shot is dropped from every live approach bucket.
- No v3 around-green generator picks it up: ScramblingGenerator (generators/scrambling.ts:51-68) reads only `sand_save_percentage` from cache; it never surfaces a 30-50yd around-green proximity/efficiency insight.
- Cache calculator (file is at src/lib/utils/golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts, NOT the v2/ path the finding cited — minor path error, line numbers + snippets all match) confirms: approach-prox-by-distance bucket (1771: bucket=''), approach-eff-by-distance (1782: `>= AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS` i.e. >=50 skips it), and ATG efficiency (1855: `s.shot_type === 'around_green'` excludes it). AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS=50 (line 519).

Corroborated by the design spec itself: docs/fairway-coachhelm-insight-rebuild.md:40 documents this exact gap — "attribution mismatch (input tags <=30 yd vs calc counts 50 yd-from-hole, use-shot-state-machine.ts:866 vs calc:471-486)" — and GAP #7 (line 66) calls to reconcile band edges to one set. So this is a documented, known issue, not speculation.

Domain lens: docs/v3-research-golf-domain.md:22-23 defines APP as ">~30 yds" and ARG as "within ~30 yds" (from green edge); the spec line 40 names "long chips (20-30 yd) leak" as a real coachable category, and 30-50yd partial wedges are a recognized distinct skill. A player weak from 40yd would indeed get no by-distance cause in either theme. This is a genuine coaching blind spot.

Two reasons it is NOT critical and sits at the medium/high boundary: (1) The finding's claim that "approach-proximity counts/averages are understated" is imprecise — calc line 1745 pushes hole.approachProximity to the OVERALL approach average regardless of distance bucket, so a green-hit 40yd wedge actually pollutes (inflates) the overall approach stat rather than being dropped from it; only the by-distance/by-distance-lie buckets and ATG-efficiency drop it. (2) It produces MISSING coverage, not a wrong number a user acts on — no fabricated value. The affected cache fields atgEfficiency*/approachEffByDistance* are not consumed anywhere on the live coachhelm/golf path (grep returned nothing), and scrambling SUCCESS rate still captures these shots via the distance-fallback at calc line 873. So the live user-facing damage is the narrow-band silent exclusion from v3 approach-by-distance buckets plus the absence of any <50yd short-game by-distance insight.

Net: real, reproducible, live, domain-relevant, but a narrow band with partial mitigations and no fabricated number. Materially degraded/incomplete insight rather than a wrong claim. High is slightly generous; medium-to-high. I land on medium given the partial mitigations and that it is missing-coverage not a wrong number, but it is a legitimate finding.

PARTIALLY CONFIRMED but materially overstated; I downgrade to medium. Paths corrected: calculator lives at src/lib/utils/golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts (finding cited the wrong src/lib/coachhelm/v2 path, but the code matches). AROUND_GREEN_THRESHOLD_YARDS=50 (line 519); getApproachDistanceBucket returns '' for <50 (line 480); approach-efficiency loop requires approachDistance>=50 (line 1782); ATG-efficiency loop filters strictly to shot_type==='around_green' (line 1855). Entry tags around_green only at <=30yd (use-shot-state-machine.ts:866). So there IS a genuine 31-49yd dead-zone for (a) approach-EFFICIENCY, (b) the per-distance approach-proximity BUCKET (line 1769-1771, gated by `if (bucket)`), and (c) ATG-EFFICIENCY. This exact mismatch is even documented in the spec gap list (docs/fairway-coachhelm-insight-rebuild.md:40: "input tags ≤30 yd vs calc counts 50 yd-from-hole, use-shot-state-machine.ts:866 vs calc:471-486"). That core is real and reproducible.

BUT the finding's stated IMPACT is wrong on two counts, which is what the skeptic lens catches:
1. The approach shot is selected by SHOT NUMBER (girAttemptShotNumber = par-2, lines 803-823), NOT by entry shot_type. A 40yd GIR-attempt wedge is therefore chosen as approachShot, so hole.approachDistance=40 and hole.approachProximity are set, and that proximity IS pushed into the OVERALL approachProximities average and the par/lie splits (lines 1745-1765). Only the per-distance bucket (line 1769) drops it. So "approach-proximity counts/averages are understated" is FALSE for the headline overall/par/lie proximity stats — those include the shot. The claim of understated averages is incorrect for the primary metric.
2. "Invisible to Around-the-Green proximity/efficiency stats" is overstated: the aroundGreenShot finder (line 873) and the scramble-distance fallback (line 1824-1832) both catch any non-putt/non-tee shot with distance <=50yd regardless of shot_type, so a 40yd up-and-down IS counted in scrambling %, sand saves, and scramble distance buckets. Only the dedicated ATG-EFFICIENCY loop (line 1855) drops it.

Net: the defect is real but confined to SECONDARY breakdown/efficiency matrices (approach-efficiency, per-distance proximity bucket whose lowest label '30_75' captures nothing under 50, and ATG-efficiency), not the headline averages a user primarily acts on, and the headline approach proximity is NOT understated. No wrong top-line number is produced; granularity in breakdowns is degraded and a band whose label implies 30+ silently excludes 30-49. That is medium (correctness-adjacent / robustness gap), not high. Live path confirmed (calculator feeds v3 generators/stats caches; entry path is the shot tracker). Proposed fix (reconcile to one band edge) is sound.

confirmedFindings.title: Flat insight feed ranks on strokes_impact × confidence but all v3 generators store strokes_impact:0 (real value is in evidence.counterfactual)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Flat path ranks by `Math.abs(insight.evidence?.strokes_impact ?? 0) * Math.max(0.1, insight.evidence?.confidence ?? 0)` (line 454-455) and rankScore = `impact * confidence` (line 966-968). But every v3 generator hard-codes `strokes_impact: 0` in composeContent (e.g. approach-miss.ts:203, par-type.ts:108, putt-distance.ts, scrambling.ts:109) and the base class injects the real value into evidence.counterfactual.strokes_saved_per_round, never back into strokes_impact (generator-base.ts:129-142). ApproachMiss and ParType additionally set `confidence: 0` (approach-miss.ts:205, par-type.ts:110).
confirmedFindings.impact: On the still-live flat feed (coach morning-digest cron, player-fingerprint.ts, stats-intelligence.ts, FairwayCoachHelmSignals/FairwayPlayerInsight), every v3 generator insight ranks at exactly 0 and is ordered arbitrarily; the genuinely highest-leverage diagnostic is not surfaced first. getRoundTakeawayInsight (line 567-572) picks the wrong takeaway card for the same reason.
confirmedFindings.fix: Rank the flat path on evidence.counterfactual.strokes_saved_per_round (fallback to strokes_impact) as the spec gap #5 prescribes, or copy strokes_saved_per_round into evidence.strokes_impact in generator-base.ts after computeCounterfactual so both paths agree.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced every cited claim from the actual code.

RANKING (read path, LIVE): insight-delivery.ts:453-456 ranks the flat coach feed by `Math.abs(insight.evidence?.strokes_impact ?? 0) * Math.max(0.1, insight.evidence?.confidence ?? 0)`; insight-delivery.ts:965-968 `rankScore` = `Math.abs(Number(insight.evidence.strokes_impact ?? 0)) * Number(insight.evidence.confidence ?? 0)`. getTopInsightForPlayer (line 241-244), getInsightsForPlayer (line 356), getInsightsForCoach (line 450-457), and getRoundTakeawayInsight (line 515, 570) all sort on this. The DB query orders by created_at DESC then re-sorts client-side, so ties collapse to arbitrary created_at order.

GENERATORS store 0: confirmed approach-miss.ts:203 `strokes_impact: 0` + :205 `confidence: 0`; par-type.ts:108/110; putt-distance.ts:138/140; scrambling.ts:109/111 — all hardcode `strokes_impact: 0` and `confidence: 0`.

BASE CLASS (engine/generator-base.ts, finding mistyped the dir as generators/ but the line numbers match): lines 129-142 spread `...composed.evidence` (carrying strokes_impact:0) and add only `standing` + `counterfactual`; it never copies counterfactual.strokes_saved_per_round into strokes_impact and never overwrites confidence. upsert-v3.ts persists evidence as-is (no remap). ApproachMiss has requiresStanding=false (approach-miss.ts:110) so it skips the injection block entirely — persists strokes_impact:0, confidence:0, NO counterfactual. ParType/Scrambling/PuttDistance inherit requiresStanding=true, get a counterfactual injected, but strokes_impact stays 0.

NET EFFECT: every one of the 9 Tier-1 v3 generator insights persists rankScore = 0*x = 0. mapRowToEvidenceInsight (line 906-907) keeps them (0 is a number, passes the typeof guard), so they enter the feed but rank at exactly 0 and order arbitrarily among themselves. Composite rules are mixed: several DO compute real non-zero strokes_impact (front-9-starter.ts:87 delta*3, doubles-after-bogey.ts:87, closing-hole-fatigue.ts:87 delta*6, pressure-decel-chain.ts:75), so those always outrank every generator insight; other composites store 0 too. The finding's phrasing "every v3 generator insight ranks at exactly 0" is correct for the 9 generators; "ordered arbitrarily" is correct.

LIVE: confirmed consumers — coach insights page, CoachAlertCenter, InsightsFeed, player hub (getTopInsightForPlayer), round-review takeaway (getRoundTakeawayInsight), player-fingerprint.ts:271, stats-intelligence.ts:272/350, and the coach-morning-digest cron which has its own rankScore (route.ts:361-363) sorting on strokes_impact (line 355), over-fetches then slices to limit (line 332/356) — so generator insights pinned at 0 get truncated out of the digest, and the digest even emits strokes_impact (line 389), which would read 0. Not dead code, no disabled flag.

One nuance correcting the finding: it is not that the entire feed is unordered — composite rules with real numbers sort correctly. The defect is that all 9 single-discipline generators (approach/putting/scrambling/par-type) are systematically pinned at 0 and thus buried beneath any composite with a non-zero impact, and ordered arbitrarily among themselves. The counterfactual value still renders correctly from evidence.counterfactual on the card itself, so no wrong NUMBER is shown — this is misordering/burial of the highest-leverage diagnostics, not a corrupted stat.

Severity: misleading/materially-degraded insight ranking on a core live path that decides which insight is featured first and which makes the limited morning digest — high, not critical (no wrong number a user acts on, no data loss). Matches claimed severity.

Verified the core mechanism in the live code. The flat read path ranks on |strokes_impact| × confidence (insight-delivery.ts:453-456 in getInsightsForCoach; rankScore at :966-968 used by getTopInsightForPlayer at :244), while all 9 Tier-1 generators hard-code strokes_impact:0 in composeContent (approach-miss.ts:203, par-type.ts:108, putt-distance.ts:138, scrambling.ts:109, putt-bias.ts:150, course-mgmt.ts:119/156, tee-strategy.ts:213, pressure-gap.ts:131, warmup-hole.ts:134). The base class injects the real per-round value into evidence.counterfactual and never copies it back into strokes_impact — confirmed at src/lib/coachhelm/v3/engine/generator-base.ts:129-142, where the spread `...composed.evidence` preserves the 0 and only adds `counterfactual`. par-type.ts:110 and approach-miss.ts:205 additionally set confidence:0, so those score doubly zero. The flat path is unambiguously live: consumed by the coach insights page, CoachAlertCenter, hub top card (getTopInsightForPlayer), coachhelm dashboard, round review, Fairway components, and the coach-morning-digest cron. Result: every Tier-1-generator insight ranks at exactly 0 on the flat feed, so the highest-leverage diagnostic is not surfaced first and ordering collapses to created_at recency; getTopInsightForPlayer's "feature this card" selection (line 244) picks the most-recent rather than highest-leverage insight.

Golf-domain judgment: this is a genuine coaching-quality defect, not cosmetic. The counterfactual strokes_saved_per_round (gap × stroke_impact_per_unit vs PGA baseline, compute.ts:65) IS the strokes-gained leverage signal — the entire SG premise is "fix what saves the most strokes first." Ranking the flat feed at 0 means a 1.2-stroke putting gap can be ordered below a 0.3-stroke approach gap, steering a coach toward a lower-leverage focus on the top card / alert center. The spec confirms intent (docs/fairway-coachhelm-insight-rebuild.md:23 "Causes ranked by counterfactual.strokes_saved, NOT the frequently-zero strokes_impact"; gap #5 at line 64), and the parallel themes read path (assemble.ts:280) already ranks correctly on strokes_saved_per_round — so the two read paths genuinely disagree.

Minor finding inaccuracies that do not change the substance: the base class is at engine/generator-base.ts (not generators/generator-base.ts), and lines 129-142 are the evidence-spread block rather than an explicit injection line. Also, "every v3 generator" is slightly overstated — several COMPOSITE rules set non-zero strokes_impact (front-9-starter.ts:87, closing-hole-fatigue.ts:87, pressure-decel-chain.ts:75, doubles-after-bogey.ts:87), so composite insights do rank > 0; only the 9 Tier-1 generators (the bulk of diagnostics) collapse to 0. The user-facing impact (misleading order, wrong "top" card) is real and materially degrades the insight, but it does not display a wrong number — the counterfactual line renders correctly from evidence.counterfactual. That makes it high (misleading/materially degraded), not critical.

CONFIRMED. Every load-bearing claim verified from code, and I could not find a guard that neutralizes it.

Mechanics verified:
- All 9 live v3 generators hard-code strokes_impact: 0 in composeContent (approach-miss.ts:203, par-type.ts:108, scrambling.ts:109, putt-distance.ts:138, putt-bias.ts:150, course-mgmt.ts:119/156, pressure-gap.ts:131, warmup-hole.ts:134, tee-strategy.ts:213). approach-miss.ts:205 and par-type.ts:110 additionally set confidence: 0.
- generator-base.ts:129-142 injects the real value only into evidence.counterfactual (CounterfactualProjection.strokes_saved_per_round, types.ts:18) and never copies it back into evidence.strokes_impact.
- These generators are LIVE: instantiated and .run() called in v2/orchestrator.ts:232-257 (v2 equivalents commented out as "superseded by v3"), writing rows to golf_coach_insights.
- The flat ranker reads evidence.strokes_impact: insight-delivery.ts:454-455 (getInsightsForCoach) and rankScore at 966-968 = |strokes_impact| * confidence (used by getTopInsightForPlayer:244, getRoundTakeawayInsight:515/570). So every v3 row scores exactly 0.

Skeptic attempts to kill it, all failed:
1. Urgent short-circuit (getTopInsightForPlayer:198-216) only fires for priority==='urgent'; v3 sets priority:'low' (approach-miss.ts:188). Doesn't save them.
2. mapRowToEvidenceInsight:906 drops rows where strokes_impact is non-numeric — but v3 writes the NUMBER 0, so rows survive and enter the broken ranking. Makes it worse, not better.
3. Themes path (getThemesForPlayer, assemble.ts) DOES rank on counterfactual and is the v3-correct path, BUT it is flag-gated and lives only in the player /coachhelm redesign fork (coachhelm/page.tsx:205-206 "lives ONLY in this fork so the flag-OFF path is byte-identical"). The coach /dashboard/insights page (InsightsPageContent.tsx) has NO themes/flag fork at all and uses getInsightsForCoach's flat ordering unconditionally. The coach-morning-digest cron (vercel.json:58-59, scheduled daily 30 6 * * *) re-implements rankScore as impact*confidence (route.ts:363) and emits the strokes_impact field directly (route.ts:384-389), so the digest email literally reports "0 strokes" and mis-orders v3 diagnostics. Flat path is live, multi-consumer.
4. This is a spec-acknowledged GAP, not speculation: docs/fairway-coachhelm-insight-rebuild.md:13/23/64 explicitly note strokes_impact is "frequently-zero" and prescribe ranking by counterfactual.

Minor overstatement (does not change severity): "ordered arbitrarily" is imprecise. V8/Node Array.sort is stable, so all-zero scores preserve the DB's created_at DESC order — the feed degrades to recency-ordered, not random. The substantive harm holds: the highest-leverage diagnostic is not surfaced first, and the daily digest email shows 0 strokes for real diagnostics.

Severity: high is correct. It does not corrupt a stroke number inside a single card (each card's own counterfactual line is right), so not critical; but it misleads selection/ordering across a live coach feed + a live daily digest email coaches act on, and surfaces "0 strokes" in that email — materially degraded insight surfacing. Claimed high/0.9/live all hold.

confirmedFindings.title: PuttBias drill tags exist only for high/low (never generated); the left/right insights that ARE generated have no drills → broken plan CTA
confirmedFindings.evidence: Generator only ever emits left/right: `const DIR_TO_METRIC_ID: Record<Exclude<BreakDirection,'straight'>, MetricId> = { left: 'putt_miss_bias_left_pct', right: 'putt_miss_bias_right_pct' }` and `constructor(... weakestDirection: 'left'|'right' = 'left')`. But the drill seed tags only the OTHER two: `impacts_metric_id = 'putt_miss_bias_high_pct' WHERE slug='putt_high_side_preference'` and `'putt_miss_bias_low_pct' WHERE slug='putt_low_side_discipline'` (supabase/migrations_archive/.../20260526060000_v3_seed_drill_metric_tags.sql) — no left/right drill rows.
confirmedFindings.impact: A generated 'putt miss bias' cause (metric putt_miss_bias_left_pct/right_pct) joins to zero golf_drills, so its development-plan leaf is empty: 'Make this a focus area' produces a goal with no Practice-Rx drills. confirmedFindings.fix: Add golf_drills.impacts_metric_id tags for putt_miss_bias_left_pct and putt_miss_bias_right_pct (face/start-line drills), since those are the only bias metrics the generator produces. The high/low tags currently point at metrics no generator emits.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced the full chain from source.

(1) GENERATOR (putt-bias.ts:45-48): `const DIR_TO_METRIC_ID: Record<Exclude<BreakDirection,'straight'>, MetricId> = { left: 'putt_miss_bias_left_pct', right: 'putt_miss_bias_right_pct' }` — only left/right. Constructor (putt-bias.ts:59-61): `constructor(playerId: string, weakestDirection: 'left'|'right' = 'left')` then `this.metricId = DIR_TO_METRIC_ID[weakestDirection]`. So the only metric_ids this generator can ever attach are the left/right pair. Verbatim match to the finding.

(2) LIVE PATH CONFIRMED: PuttBiasGenerator is instantiated in src/lib/coachhelm/v2/orchestrator.ts:236-237 inside the `tier1Generators` array: `{ name: 'v3.puttBias.left', fn: () => new PuttBiasGenerator(playerId, 'left').run() }` and `'v3.puttBias.right' ... 'right'`. This array is executed via Promise.allSettled (orchestrator.ts:271). This orchestrator is `coachHelmIntelligence.analyzePlayer`, which generateInsightsForTeam calls (insights.ts:833) and the post-round trigger calls. No 'high'/'low' instantiation exists anywhere (grep confirms only .left/.right). So left/right putt-bias insights are genuinely produced; high/low are dead metric_ids.

(3) SEED INVERTED (supabase/migrations_archive/pre_20260527/20260526060000_v3_seed_drill_metric_tags.sql:32-33): `UPDATE public.golf_drills SET impacts_metric_id = 'putt_miss_bias_high_pct' WHERE slug = 'putt_high_side_preference';` and `... 'putt_miss_bias_low_pct' WHERE slug = 'putt_low_side_discipline';`. No rows tag putt_miss_bias_left_pct or putt_miss_bias_right_pct. Verbatim match.

(4) BROKEN CTA (src/app/golf/actions/v3/practice-rx.ts:39-56): candidate drills are `.eq('impacts_metric_id', goal.metric_id)`; if `candidate_drills.length === 0` it returns `{ ok: false, error: 'No drills tagged with impacts_metric_id=...' }`. A goal created from a putt-bias insight carries metric_id = putt_miss_bias_left_pct/right_pct (goals.ts:121 inserts input.metric_id), which has zero tagged drills → empty Practice-Rx leaf. Confirmed.

Caveats (don't change verdict, support claimed medium): PuttBias has requiresStanding=false and strokes_impact:0 (putt-bias.ts:150,55), so it does NOT flow through the standing-driven auto-goal suggestion-writer.ts path (which filters by metricsWithDrillCoverage at suggestion-writer.ts:202-204). The break only surfaces when a user/coach manually elevates a putt-bias insight to a focus area and requests Practice-Rx — a degraded plan leaf, not a wrong number a user acts on. Minor framing nit: the high/low tags are valid registry metrics, just orphaned; the real gap is the missing left/right tags. Both the issue and its live-path status are confirmed.

VERIFIED MECHANICS (all file:line confirmed):

1. Generator only emits left/right. src/lib/coachhelm/v3/generators/putt-bias.ts:45-48 `const DIR_TO_METRIC_ID: Record<Exclude<BreakDirection,'straight'>, MetricId> = { left: 'putt_miss_bias_left_pct', right: 'putt_miss_bias_right_pct' }` and constructor at :59 takes only 'left'|'right'.

2. Generator IS live. src/lib/coachhelm/v2/orchestrator.ts:236-237 instantiates `new PuttBiasGenerator(playerId, 'left').run()` and `...(playerId, 'right').run()`. So the only bias metrics ever produced are left/right.

3. Drill seed tags only high/low. supabase/migrations_archive/pre_20260527/20260526060000_v3_seed_drill_metric_tags.sql:32-33 sets `impacts_metric_id='putt_miss_bias_high_pct' WHERE slug='putt_high_side_preference'` and `='putt_miss_bias_low_pct' WHERE slug='putt_low_side_discipline'`. grep across supabase/ confirms NO row tags putt_miss_bias_left_pct or putt_miss_bias_right_pct. The high/low metrics are seeded in the registry/PGA tables but no generator emits them — so the tags point at orphan metrics, and the live metrics (left/right) have zero drill coverage. (Active baseline 20260527000000 only defines the column/FK/index; the seed lives in the archived migration, but the impacts_metric_id→drill model is current — practice-rx.ts and suggestion-writer.ts both query it live.)

4. Practice-Rx joins on impacts_metric_id and hard-fails on zero matches. src/app/golf/actions/v3/practice-rx.ts:42 `.eq('impacts_metric_id', goal.metric_id)` then :51-56 `if (candidate_drills.length === 0) return { ok:false, error: 'No drills tagged with impacts_metric_id=${goal.metric_id}...' }`. So a goal with metric_id=putt_miss_bias_left_pct/right_pct can never get a Practice Rx; it returns a developer-facing error string verbatim.

5. The CTA reaching this is gated only on metric existence, not drill coverage. src/lib/coachhelm/v3/themes/assemble.ts:521 `canMakePlan: metric != null`. handleMakePlan in src/components/fairway/pages/coachhelm/FairwayPlayerCoachHelm.tsx:327-338 passes `metric_id: cause.metric` straight into createGoal, which accepts any valid MetricId (src/app/golf/actions/v3/goals.ts:54-56). So a putt-bias cause's 'Add to development plan' creates the goal fine, and the downstream Practice Rx for that goal then errors. The reachable failure is REAL.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING'S FRAMING:
- It says the plan leaf shows a graceful 'no drill yet — talk to your coach' fallback. Actual behavior is a hard ok:false with a raw internal string exposed (practice-rx.ts:54). The goal IS created (createGoal succeeds); it's the separate Practice-Rx step that breaks. The finding slightly overstates/mis-describes the exact UX.
- It conflates the inline drill-CHIP mechanism with impacts_metric_id. Inline chips come from golf_insight_drill_attachments (insight-delivery.ts:158-160), populated by category+tags overlap in v2 upsert.ts:429-433 (attachDrills), NOT by impacts_metric_id and NOT invoked by the v3 putt-bias generator. So putt-bias insights have no inline chips for a different reason. The Practice-Rx/goal path is the one impacts_metric_id governs.
- The auto goal-suggestion writer (suggestion-writer.ts:102) self-protects: it skips metrics without drill coverage and reads golf_player_standing, which putt-bias (requiresStanding=false) is absent from. So only the manual cause-CTA path triggers this, not the cron suggester. This narrows blast radius.

GOLF-DOMAIN LENS: No wrong coaching NUMBER and no false claim. The putt-bias insight's diagnostic (make-% by break direction vs the player's own straight-putt baseline) is accurate and domain-sensible. The research doc has no putt-miss-bias guidance, so there is no domain-truth violation. This is a data-coverage/broken-CTA robustness defect: a player who clicks 'add to plan' on a putt-bias insight ends up with a development-plan goal that can never produce a practice plan (raw error surfaced). That is a materially degraded experience for one insight type, not a correctness-of-numbers issue.

Net: core defect is confirmed and reproducible; severity medium is correct (degraded/broken insight CTA, not a wrong number or data loss). The finding's title/impact wording is partly inaccurate but the substantive bug and its fix (tag left/right drills; the high/low tags are dead) hold.

The data-layer mismatch is REAL and reproducible: PuttBiasGenerator only emits putt_miss_bias_left_pct/right_pct (putt-bias.ts:45-48 DIR_TO_METRIC_ID maps only left/right; constructor :59-61 accepts only 'left'|'right'), while the LIVE baseline migration tags drills only for high/low — supabase/migrations/20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql:32-33 ("UPDATE golf_drills SET impacts_metric_id='putt_miss_bias_high_pct' WHERE slug='putt_high_side_preference'" and the low equivalent). Zero left/right drill rows exist, so a metric-filtered drill query for either emitted metric returns nothing. (Note: the finding cited the archived seed at migrations_archive/.../20260526060000; the same defect persists in the live baseline, so the citation is correct in substance.)

But the claimed user-facing impact — "every bias insight's development-plan leaf is empty / broken 'Make this a focus area' CTA" — is neutralized by three guards/gaps:

1) Engine goal-suggestion path is guarded against exactly this: suggestion-writer.ts:102 "if (!input.metricsWithDrillCoverage.has(row.metric_id)) continue;" skips uncovered metrics, and it sources from golf_player_standing only. The generator sets requiresStanding=false (putt-bias.ts:55, "No PGA standing exists for putt-bias metrics"), so bias metrics never get standing rows and are never auto-suggested as goals.

2) No insight CTA pre-seeds a bias-metric goal. The v3 GoalCreationModal (the only UI writer of golf_goals) is opened with no initialMetricId at fairway/pages/coachhelm/GoalsSection.tsx:276, defaulting to 'sg_putting' (GoalCreationModal/index.tsx:64). grep "initialMetricId=" returns zero callers. The real insight→focus CTA, PromoteToFocusAreaButton (source='insight'), calls createFocusAreaFromInsightV2 which writes the V2 golf_player_focus_areas table with a FREE-TEXT targetMetric (placeholders "e.g. 3-putt %") and never touches golf_drills.impacts_metric_id — so it cannot produce the empty-plan outcome the finding describes.

3) The only code that performs the impacts_metric_id=goal.metric_id drill join and returns the hard "No drills tagged" error — generatePracticeRx in app/golf/actions/v3/practice-rx.ts:39-56 — has ZERO callers anywhere in src/ (grep confirms; the PracticePlan references in components are a separate prescribed-plan card with a generic empty state at PrescribedPracticePlanCard.tsx:415, not this join).

So reaching the broken outcome requires a user to manually open the generic "New goal" form, scroll the dropdown to "Putt Miss Left %", create the goal, and trigger a Practice Rx surface that isn't wired. The finding's headline ("every bias insight will show an empty plan / fallback") is not supported. The underlying tag mismatch is a genuine latent data-seed defect that will matter once Practice Rx is wired, but it is not a live user-facing break today. Live=false in practice (unreachable), and severity is overstated. Lowering to low.

confirmedFindings.title: College/division baseline (standing.level_avg) is fetched but the counterfactual is hard-anchored to PGA Tour for every player
confirmedFindings.evidence: cfInput passes only `pga_value: standing.pga_value` (line 123) into computeCounterfactual, which accepts no cohort field (compute.ts:27-35 `pga_value: number`). The standing row DOES carry division data — loader.ts:19-21 selects `level_avg, level_n, level_pct` — and pga-standards.ts:120-133 cohortBaselineValue exists with the comment 'Used by W17 counterfactual so a D3 player's target is realistic (D3 avg, not Tour)'. verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from source on the live path. CONFIRMED facts:

(1) generator-base.ts:119-126 builds cfInput passing ONLY `pga_value: standing.pga_value` (line 123) into computeCounterfactual. The ComputeCounterfactualInput interface has no cohort field — compute.ts:31 `player_value: number` / compute.ts:32 `pga_value: number` only. The gap is computed strictly against pga_value (compute.ts:53-55 `gap = direction === 'higher_better' ? input.pga_value - input.player_value : input.player_value - input.pga_value`) and the displayed projection is gap-to-Tour (compute.ts:91 `projected_score_if_closed: input.player_30d_scoring_avg - strokes_saved_per_round`).

(2) The standing row DOES carry division/cohort data — loader.ts:19-21 SELECT_FIELDS includes `level_avg, level_n, level_pct`, typed in RawRow (loader.ts:30-32). A repo-wide grep shows level_avg/level_pct/level_n have ZERO consumers anywhere in src/ except the loader, types, and database.ts schema (the other matches are the unrelated `hole_level_avg` metric-source concept in causality/).

(3) cohortBaselineValue + CohortTier exist (pga-standards.ts:120-133, type at :20) with the exact documented comment 'Used by W17 counterfactual so a D3 player's "close the gap" target is realistic (D3 avg, not Tour)...' but grep confirms they are NEVER called — only self-references inside pga-standards.ts. So the doc comment is inaccurate (it claims active use).

LIVE-PATH verified: concrete Tier-1 generators extend BaseGenerator (e.g. scrambling.ts, putt-distance.ts, par-type.ts) and default requiresStanding=true, which triggers the computeCounterfactual injection block (generator-base.ts:114-127). generateInsightsForTeam runs these generators. The PGA-anchored counterfactual reaches a user-facing surface: the /dashboard/my-standing page renders CounterfactualLine (page.tsx:232-240) fed `pga_value={standing.pga_value}` directly, which calls formatCounterfactualLine → 'Closing this gap → X → Y (≈N wks)' where Y is the gap-to-Tour. For a D2/D3 player this overstates the realistic improvement target/stroke savings.

The finding's stated nuance is also accurate: the themes assembler DOES separately compute a team-anchored 'realistic' number via realisticTeamGap (assemble.ts:108-125, used at :448/:479/:501) for cause ranking/sizing — so the theme-tree stroke values are team-discounted — but the CounterfactualLine secondary line on my-standing still shows the raw PGA-anchored projection. So the impact is real but partially mitigated in the themes layer.

This is not a hard-wrong number (it is correctly the gap-to-PGA-Tour), but it is a misleading development target for non-PGA-track players, and the cohort-aware infrastructure to fix it is built but orphaned. Matches documented spec gap #8 (college-primary, Tour ceiling). Medium severity is well-calibrated.

Mechanically and domain-wise confirmed on the live path. Verified evidence:

1. generator-base.ts:119-126 builds cfInput with only `pga_value: standing.pga_value` (line 123) plus player_value and the 30d baseline; computeCounterfactual (compute.ts:27-35) has no cohort/division field, so the gap is hard-anchored to PGA Tour: `gap = pga_value - player_value` (compute.ts:53-55).
2. The standing row DOES carry division data — loader.ts:21,30 selects/types `level_avg, level_n, level_pct`, and PlayerStanding.level_avg exists (types.ts:24) — but a grep shows `level_avg` is never read by any insight consumer (the only other matches are the unrelated `hole_level_avg` causality kind and the DB type). cohortBaselineValue (pga-standards.ts:120-133) and its `CohortTier` (pga-standards.ts:20) are defined with the explicit comment "Used by W17 counterfactual so a D3 player's target is realistic (D3 avg, not Tour)" but are called NOWHERE (only their own definitions appear in grep). So the cohort machinery is genuinely orphaned.
3. The PGA-anchored counterfactual reaches a real, live user surface: /dashboard/my-standing/page.tsx:232-240 (a full route with error.tsx/loading.tsx, revalidate=300, redirect-gated for auth) feeds `pga_value={standing.pga_value}` + `player_30d_scoring_avg={playerBaseline}` into CounterfactualLine, which calls computeCounterfactual and renders formatCounterfactualLine → "Closing this gap → 75.2 → 74.5 (≈4 wks)" (compute.ts:91,119-126). For a D2/D3 player the gap-to-Tour is large, so the projected score and stroke savings overstate the realistic achievable target. The domain doc is explicit: "Baselines must be context-aware — college baselines... not Tour baselines for player comparison" (v3-research-golf-domain.md:348-350), and D3 realistic scoring is "mid 70s" not ~72 (lines 100-104). The spec independently flags this as GAP #8 "Pick ONE baseline source per card — college-primary, Tour ceiling ... generators currently hard-code PGA" (fairway-coachhelm-insight-rebuild.md:67) and GAP-CLOSER #9 "switch defaults to college baseline" (line 81). So this is a documented, reproducible domain gap, not speculation.

One refinement to the finding's impact narrative (does not refute it): the PRIMARY insight surface is the ThemeCard, whose headline stroke number uses the team-anchored REALISTIC value (assemble.ts:108-125 realisticTeamGap; ThemeCard.tsx:95,121 "~X strokes/round to reach your team avg") and frames Tour as a separate, smaller secondary "ceiling" line — so the worst Tour-anchored overstatement is confined to the secondary /dashboard/my-standing CounterfactualLine, not the main coachhelm/insights theme cards. The finding already acknowledges the assembler uses team_avg for its realistic sizing. This caps the blast radius and keeps severity at medium rather than high.

Severity assessment: a real number a player/coach could act on (projected score + stroke savings) is computed against the Tour ceiling instead of the player's division, but (a) it is confined to a secondary standing-strip surface and (b) the primary theme-card number is independently team-anchored and correct. Claimed medium is the right rating. The proposed fix (pass standing.level_avg, or cohortBaselineValue by division, as the baseline with PGA fallback) matches both the domain doc and the spec gap.

Independently verified and the core claim holds, though with caveats that keep it at medium (not higher).

CONFIRMED on the live path:
- generator-base.ts:123 passes only `pga_value: standing.pga_value` into the cfInput; ComputeCounterfactualInput (compute.ts:27-35) has no cohort/division field, so the counterfactual gap is computed strictly against PGA Tour (compute.ts:53-55, projected_score_if_closed at compute.ts:91 is gap-to-Tour).

WHERE THE FINDING IS OVERSTATED / fix is incomplete (skeptic findings):
1. The proposed fix (pass standing.level_avg) is a NO-OP today. The refresh_player_standing SQL function (migration 20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql:4689-4710) never inserts level_avg/level_n/level_pct, and its pga CTE (lines 4682-4688) only reads pga_tour_value/pga_p50 — so level_avg is always NULL in golf_player_standing despite loader.ts:21 selecting it. confirmedFindings.title: v3 loadApproachShots never fetches distance_unit_before; bucketApproachDistance assumes yards, so a feet-entered approach is misbucketed
confirmedFindings.evidence: loadApproachShots selects `distance_to_hole_before` WITHOUT distance_unit_before (line 102), and the ApproachShot interface comments it `// yards` (line 25). bucketApproachDistance treats the raw number as yards: `if (yards >= 50 && yards < 125) ...` (line 70). Likely rare (approaches are usually entered in yards), hence lower confidence/severity.
confirmedFindings.fix: Fetch distance_unit_before in loadApproachShots and normalize to yards before bucketApproachDistance (mirror stats-data.ts:953-959), so the v3 shot-source and the calculator agree on units.

confirmedFindings.title: short_side_scrambling_chain & flyer_lie chains consume proximity as feet with no unit normalization or test
confirmedFindings.evidence: loadShortGameShots/loadFlyerLieShots select `'round_id, hole_number, lie_before, distance_to_hole_before, distance_to_hole_after'` — NOT distance_unit_after — and return the raw value. The chains compare it to feet thresholds: short-side-scrambling-chain.ts:29-31 `avgProximity ... if (avgProximity <= POOR_PROXIMITY_FT)` (15), flyer-lie-over-the-green.ts:33-35 (>35), both with `unit:'feet'`. shot-source.ts:26 documents distance_to_hole_after as 'raw, in the unit named by distance_unit_after — normalize to feet before use'. The invariant is structurally guaranteed in code, not just by example. assemble.ts:501-502: `strokesSavedPerRound = ownsLeaves ? compositeSameCategoryStrokes : ownRealistic` and `finalTourGapPerRound = ownsLeaves ? compositeSameCategoryTourGap : tourGapPerRound`. For a non-composite, `ownRealistic = realisticTeamGap(tourGap, standing)` (line 448) which returns either `tourGap` (line 119, no team data) or `tourGap * teamFraction` where `teamFraction = clamp01(...)` ∈ [0,1] (lines 123-124). For non-negative tourGap that is provably ≤ tourGap. Composites sum term-wise-bounded leaves (lines 479-480: each leaf's realisticTeamGap ≤ its leafTourGap). Theme level uses `Math.min(realisticChildSum, |sg|)` (line 309) and sums leaf tourGaps (line 317). So realistic ≤ Tour is an algebraic identity for tourGap ≥ 0.

2. The ONLY way to breach it is a negative tourGap (negative × [0,1]-fraction yields a value greater than the negative). But negative gaps are gated out upstream on the live path: computeCounterfactual returns early at `if (gap <= 0)` (compute.ts:58), and marks anything below the 0.3 threshold (which subsumes all negatives) as `suppressed: true` (compute.ts:67). Then tourGapOf (assemble.ts:407-414) returns the value ONLY when `cf.suppressed !== true`, else null → realisticTeamGap(null) = 0. So a negative tourGap cannot reach the comparison in production.

3. THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD CATCH NOTHING. rowsArb (assemble.test.ts:1091) generates `strokesSaved: fc.double({ min: 0, max: 5 })` — strictly non-negative — and builds rows via `row({...})` with NO standingPlayer/standingPga/team_avg, so every property-space row has `standing` undefined and realisticTeamGap always falls back to the full tourGap (teamFraction = 1), making realistic === tourGap by identity. A property asserting `realistic <= tourGap + eps` over rowsArb would pass trivially and explore exactly zero of the risky region (negative gaps + team-fraction < 1, which only appears via rowWithTeam in hand-written tests). The fix as written is decorative, not protective.

NET: This is a genuine but minor test-coverage observation (a property over the team-fraction/negative space would be more rigorous than one fixture). It is NOT correctness-adjacent at medium: there is no reachable wrong number a user acts on, the live code structurally upholds the invariant via the compute.ts gap-gate + suppress-threshold + tourGapOf-suppression chain, and the proposed property adds no real coverage without also extending the arbitrary (which the fix does not propose). Confidence in my structural/guard analysis ~0.85; I mark verdict uncertain rather than fully refuted because the descriptive coverage gap is real, just over-rated.

contestedFindings.title: approach-category composites (long_approach_3putt, short_approach_gap) own a same-category leaf (approach_miss) that has no counterfactual → composite sizes to 0 strokes
contestedFindings.evidence: buildCause sizes a composite from its demoted same-category leaves: `compositeSameCategoryStrokes += realisticTeamGap(leafTourGap, ...)`. For long_approach_3putt_cascade (category 'approach'), its same-category leaf is the approach_miss row, which is requiresStanding=false (approach-miss.ts:110) so it carries no evidence.counterfactual → tourGapOf(leafEv)=null → realisticTeamGap=0. The cross-category putt leaf is excluded by the `leaf.category === category` guard (assemble.ts:476). So compositeSameCategoryStrokes=0 and strokesSavedPerRound=0.
contestedFindings.impact: When long_approach_3putt_cascade / short_approach_proximity_gap do fire, they render as a 0-stroke 'Tendency' cause in the Approach / Around-the-Green theme — the synthesized 'long approach → 3-putt' chain shows no addressable strokes even though it is framed as urgent/high. contestedFindings.fix: Same remedy family: give approach_miss a real counterfactual (populate the deferred approach_proximity standing) or let the composite fall back to its own evidence.strokes_impact when its leaves yield 0. Without it the approach composites are quantitatively empty.

verdicts.reasoning:

- realisticTeamGap (assemble.ts:112): `if (tourGap == null || !Number.isFinite(tourGap)) return 0;`

- approach-miss.ts:110 `protected override readonly requiresStanding = false;` → generator-base.ts:114 wraps counterfactual+standing injection in `if (standing)`, and standing is null for requiresStanding=false generators (generator-base.ts:98-100). Mechanism CONFIRMED for ONE of the two named composites, REFUTED for the other.

CONFIRMED — long_approach_3putt_cascade: rule has category 'approach' (long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts:36) and claims leaves [longApproach (approach_miss, category 'approach'), midPutt (putt_distance, category 'putting')] (lines 43). Its same-category owned leaf is therefore the SCRAMBLING leaf (scrambling.ts:39 category 'short_game'), which inherits the default requiresStanding=true (scrambling.ts:7) and DOES carry a counterfactual. The approach_miss leaf is the cross-category one (excluded). So this composite sizes correctly from the scrambling leaf's realistic gap. The finding incorrectly lumped this composite in.

IMPACT correction (softens severity): the finding says it renders as a "0-stroke 'Tendency'" implying a misleading number. The cascade prose and the linked putt driver still render (lines 208, 215). So the user does NOT see a fabricated/wrong "0.0 strokes saved" claim — they see graceful, honest degradation.

GOLF-DOMAIN verdict: the long approach → mid-range putt → 3-putt cascade is a real, valuable causal chain (domain doc line 351 explicitly allows "lag distance drives 3-putt rate" type causal claims). Net: the underlying mechanism and live-path claim are real for long_approach_3putt_cascade; the second composite citation is a false positive; the user-facing impact is "valuable insight de-quantified + un-plannable" (honest degradation), correctly rated medium. Partly real, materially overstated, and factually wrong on one of its two named composites.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED: For `long_approach_3putt_cascade` only (rule `category: 'approach'`, long-approach-3putt-cascade.ts:36), the engine does size the cause to 0 strokes via a counterfactual-less leaf. Chain verified: approach_miss generator sets `requiresStanding = false` (approach-miss.ts:110); generator-base.ts:98-114 only injects `standing`+`counterfactual` inside the `if (standing)` block, so an approach_miss row carries NO `evidence.counterfactual`. The composite still OWNS that same-category leaf (assemble.ts:476, leaf.category 'approach' === composite category 'approach'), so `ownsLeaves = true` (assemble.ts:500) and `strokesSavedPerRound = compositeSameCategoryStrokes = 0` (assemble.ts:501). WHY THE FINDING IS WRONG ON THE SECOND COMPOSITE: The finding asserts `short_approach_proximity_gap` is `category 'approach'` owning the approach_miss leaf. It is not. WHY NO WRONG NUMBER REACHES A USER (severity-killer): When the long_approach composite owns a zero-valued leaf, assemble.ts:515 `counterfactualSuppressed: ownsLeaves && strokesSavedPerRound > 0 ? false : ownCounterfactualSuppressed` resolves to true (strokesSavedPerRound is 0, and the composite row's own evidence has no counterfactual — synthesis.ts:114-118 writes only `strokes_impact: 0`, no counterfactual). It does NOT display "≈0.0/rd". So the user never sees a wrong/fabricated number — they see honest diagnostic degradation. The finding's "renders as a 0-stroke 'Tendency' cause" wording implies a misleading zero figure; in reality the zero is hidden behind the honest Tendency path.

KNOWN/DEFERRED, NOT A BUG: docs/fairway-coachhelm-insight-rebuild.md:33 documents this exact gap — "ApproachMissGenerator requiresStanding=false → no PGA-anchored stroke number" and names `long_approach_3putt_cascade` as the consumer. Lines 63-64 list it under "Gaps to close (Phase 2 fast-follows, not blockers): requiresStanding=false generators get no stroke number → diagnostic-only." This is an acknowledged, intentionally-deferred completeness gap, with an existing honest-fallback path, not data loss or a wrong claim.

NET: The underlying mechanism is real for ONE composite, but (a) the finding is factually wrong about the second composite (short_approach is sized from scrambling, unaffected), (b) no wrong number is shown — the suppressed/Tendency path is a deliberate honest guard that the renderer respects, and (c) the gap is documented and classified as a non-blocking fast-follow. This is correctness-adjacent completeness, not a critical/high wrong-number issue, and the claimed medium severity is inflated given the honest-degradation guard and the half-incorrect framing.

contestedFindings.title: getInsightsForPlayer applies minConfidence/window_days filters in JS AFTER the SQL limit — caller asking for N can get fewer than N even when N qualify
contestedFindings.evidence: const limit = Math.min(Math.max(opts.limit ?? 10, 1), 50); ... .limit(limit) ... then AFTER fetching: return insights.filter((insight) => { if (opts.minConfidence != null) { ... if (!Number.isFinite(confidence) || confidence < opts.minConfidence) return false; } if (opts.window_days != null) { ... } });  — the SQL limit is applied first, the confidence/window filter second.
contestedFindings.impact: Callers like stats-intelligence.getPlayerStatsIntelligence (getInsightsForPlayer(playerId,{limit:3})) and getTeamStatsIntelligence (limit:1) plus any minConfidence caller can be handed fewer rows than requested: if the newest `limit` rows are all below minConfidence, the result is empty even though qualifying rows exist just past the cut. The stats strip / team roster then shows 'no insights' for a player who has them.
contestedFindings.fix: Push minConfidence/window into the query where cheaply possible, or over-fetch (e.g. limit*4 capped at 50) before applying the JS filter and then slice to limit — mirroring the PRE_RANK_FETCH pattern getInsightsForCoach already uses.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from the actual code at /Users/ricknini/Downloads/helmv3/src/app/golf/actions/insight-delivery.ts. The SQL query applies `.limit(limit)` at line 306 (limit = Math.min(Math.max(opts.limit ?? 10, 1), 50), line 295), and the minConfidence/window_days filters are applied in JS AFTER fetch at lines 362-372: `return insights.filter((insight) => { if (opts.minConfidence != null) { ... if (!Number.isFinite(confidence) || confidence < opts.minConfidence) return false; } if (opts.window_days != null) { ... if (... windowDays > opts.window_days) return false; } ... })`. So a caller asking for N with a confidence/window filter can receive fewer than N even when N qualifying rows exist past the SQL cut. The cited PRE_RANK_FETCH contrast is also accurate: the sibling getInsightsForCoach over-fetches via `const PRE_RANK_FETCH = Math.min(50, limit * 4)` (line 408) then `ranked.slice(0, limit)` (line 465), confirming the inconsistency and the validity of the proposed fix.

LIVE PATH: confirmed. getInsightsForPlayer is exported and on the live insight-delivery path; non-test callers are stats-intelligence.ts:272 (limit:3), stats-intelligence.ts:350 (limit:1), coachhelm/page.tsx:157 (limit:6), rounds/[id]/review/page.tsx:352 (limit:6). Because the JS filters are guarded by `opts.minConfidence != null` / `opts.window_days != null`, both branches are no-ops on every current production path, so the described user-facing symptom ("stats strip / team roster shows 'no insights' for a player who has them") cannot occur today. The defect is real and on the live path, but the harm is latent: it is a footgun for the next caller that adds a filter, and an internal inconsistency vs getInsightsForCoach. That fits the rubric's "robustness gap / correctness-adjacent" = medium tier, at its low end. Verdict confirmed (the code defect exists exactly as described and is live); severity unchanged at medium, with the caveat that current real-world impact is zero until a caller passes one of those filters.

The code mechanism is real and accurately quoted: in getInsightsForPlayer the SQL `.limit(limit)` is applied at insight-delivery.ts:306 BEFORE the JS post-filter at insight-delivery.ts:362-372 (`if (opts.minConfidence != null) ... if (confidence < opts.minConfidence) return false;` and the analogous window_days branch). getInsightsForCoach by contrast uses an over-fetch pattern (`PRE_RANK_FETCH = Math.min(50, limit * 4)`, insight-delivery.ts:408), so the asymmetry the finding describes genuinely exists.

But the finding's stated user-facing IMPACT is wrong, which is decisive for severity. The bug can only fire when a caller passes `minConfidence` or `window_days`. I grepped every live call site: the two named callers do NOT pass either option — getPlayerStatsIntelligence at stats-intelligence.ts:272 calls `getInsightsForPlayer(playerId, { limit: 3 })` and getTeamStatsIntelligence at stats-intelligence.ts:350 calls `getInsightsForPlayer(pid, { limit: 1 })`. So the entire post-filter block is a no-op on every production path, and the claimed "stats strip / team roster shows 'no insights' for a player who has them" cannot happen today.

This is a latent/dormant footgun (the inline comment at lines 359-361 even mis-assumes limit=50 while live callers pass 1/3/6), worth fixing before any caller wires up the filters, but it does not degrade any insight users currently see. Verdict is uncertain because the mechanism is confirmed real while the live impact (and thus the medium rating) is refuted.

The CODE MECHANISM is real and reproducible: insight-delivery.ts:306 applies `.limit(limit)` in SQL, then lines 362-371 filter minConfidence/window_days in JS afterward — so for a caller passing those opts, the result can be shorter than `limit`. When those opts are absent, `opts.minConfidence != null` / `opts.window_days != null` are both false, so the post-fetch `.filter()` is a no-op returning exactly `limit` rows. The finding's "impact" paragraph specifically names getPlayerStatsIntelligence (limit:3) and getTeamStatsIntelligence (limit:1) as victims that could 'show no insights' — but those callers cannot trigger it because they pass no minConfidence. contestedFindings.title: v2 calculator putt/approach band edges do not reconcile with v3 registry buckets (rebuild GAP #7) — root cause of missing standing for 15-25/25+ putt and proximity buckets
contestedFindings.evidence: getPuttDistanceBucket returns `0_3 / 3_5 / 5_10 / 10_15 / 15_20 / 20_25 / 25_30 / 30_35 / 35_plus`; getApproachDistanceBucket returns 25-yd bands `30_75 / 75_100 / 100_125 / 125_150 / 150_175 / 175_200 / 200_225 / 225_plus`. The v3 registry/metric-config uses putt buckets `3_5 / 5_10 / 10_15 / 15_25 / 25_plus` (metric-config.ts:42-46) and approach buckets `50_125 / 125_175 / 175_plus` (approach-miss.ts:46-50). The calculator has no 15_25 putt band and no 50_125/125_175 approach band, so the v3 15-25/25+ putt and approach-proximity metrics never get cache-aligned standing rows. Rebuild GAP #7: 'Reconcile band edges to ONE set ... before nesting.'
contestedFindings.impact: Two whole putt buckets (15-25, 25+ — the lag-distance zone that the doc says dominates 3-putt avoidance) and all approach-proximity metrics ship with no standing bar and no stroke value; the lag_distance_3putt composite's 15+ ft child can never be produced from a v3 row, making that 'urgent' 3-putt chain near-dead on pure-v3 data.
contestedFindings.fix: Pick one canonical band set across calculator + registry + leak-map and re-key the cache columns / standing RPC to it (collapse 15_20+20_25 -> 15_25, add 50_125/125_175 approach aggregates), so the lag-putting and proximity metrics get standing and the composites can fire.

verdicts.reasoning:

The v3 standing/generation path does NOT consume those calculator functions: a repo-wide grep shows ZERO v3 importers of getPuttDistanceBucket/getApproachDistanceBucket (only v2 stats UI + the GolfStats type import them). The v3 putt-distance generator reads golf_player_stats_cache columns putt_make_pct_3_5ft/5_10ft/10_15ft directly (putt-distance.ts:41-45); the approach generator buckets raw shots via its own bucketApproachDistance in engine/shot-source.ts:69-74 with requiresStanding=false (approach-miss.ts:110); and standing rows come from golf_player_standing populated by the refresh_player_standing PL/pgSQL RPC (loader.ts:56), not the calculator. The finding's core observable (no v3 standing rows for putts_made_15_25ft_pct / 25_plus and the three approach_proximity metrics; the lag_distance_3putt composite's 15+ft child cannot be produced on pure-v3 data) is REAL and corroborated by code — but it is a KNOWN, SELF-DOCUMENTED gap with guards, and the finding mis-attributes the root cause and overstates the impact.

1. Mis-located root cause. The cited file golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:464-489 (getPuttDistanceBucket / getApproachDistanceBucket strings) is NOT what the v3 standing path keys on. Standing is populated by the refresh_player_standing() SQL RPC from NAMED cache columns, and generators read named cache columns (putt-distance.ts:41-45 BUCKET_TO_CACHE_COLUMN = putt_make_pct_3_5ft etc.). The real cache columns are putt_make_pct_15_20ft / putt_make_pct_20_plus_ft (database.ts:8119-8120), which actually DO align with the calculator's 15_20/20_25 bands — the calculator and cache are consistent with each other. The true fork is cache-band(15_20/20+) vs v3 registry-metric-id(15_25/25+), not the calculator file.

Guards neutralize any wrong-number risk: src/lib/coachhelm/v3/causality/metric-sources.ts:169-170 marks both 15_25/25_plus as kind:'intentional-null' reason:'no-per-round-putt-distance-cache'; loader.ts:67 returns null on missing rows; approach-miss.ts:110 sets requiresStanding=false and uses its own hardcoded Tour anchors. Net: real but overstated, a documented gap with guards rather than a user-facing wrong number, and the root-cause file is not load-bearing. Severity should drop from medium to low.
